title: The Connected Educator: Learning and Leading in a Digital Age
text:
I don't lightly rate books "I love it", but in The Connected Educator, Sheryl Nussbaum-Beach and Lani Ritter Hall practice the connected learning and leading of which they speak.

Prior to reading this book, I had been becoming a connected educator for almost two years. Then I found Sheryl and Lani hosting this book in a book study for Connected Educator Month, 2012. I joined in the study as much as I was able, since it was the start of a new school year, but watching them at work connecting and learning with those in the community cemented the learning for me.

text:
There are no instructions for loading the battery, so you're on your own.

My attempt began with pushing-in on the little button on the one muff. It looks like you would push in on the button, and then pull-up on the oval plastic disk just above the button. But nooooo!

Push down on that button, and at the same time SLIDE the plastic shroud below there downward a little. It's on a hinge, so don't make the mistake of yanking it off!

Rotate the shroud up and out of the way to install the battery. The flat side of the battery goes in first, with the positive terminal facing out as you push it in there. With mine, the battery supplied was dead, so I tried another and it works fine. No issues with the battery not fitting. Fits well.

I wonder how many customers will try it with the supplied "dead" battery, assume the headphones are defective, and return the unit immediately? Probably many will. It DID cross my mind. Good thing I had a few AAA batteries around here.

A few words of instructions to install the battery would be helpful. Might save them some expense for returned items, too, making it extremely cost effective. Doh!

The Koss come in a square case that houses the removable cord (it removes from the headphone and the playing device - more on that in a moment). Just above the ears is a "L" or "R" to help you figure out which way to wear them and folding them up is a breeze. It also comes with a 1/4" stereo headphone adapter.

As for that removable 3.5mm stereo plug, it can plug into the left OR the right ear and because there is a plug on both you can plug in another 3.5mm plug and have someone Join you. I did it with my Sennheisers! So I started the music and plugged my Koss' into the computer, then had my friend plug the Senns into the left (one I wasn't using) hole in the ear piece and BAM, we were both listening to really good and LOUD music! That feature is awesome!

I'm completely impressed and really pleased with these as a legitimate and lighter weight replacement for my Senns.

title: Even withstands washing machines
text:
I’ll be honest: I bought this desk mat primarily because it was large enough to cover my whole workspace and had a clean, professional look. What I did not expect was that it would survive a full cycle in my washing machine wash – including the spin dry – without any warping, fading, or peeling of the edges. I know that sounds crazy, but here is the story.

I was moving my office to a new room and, in the chaos, my mat ended up in a pile of the laundry pile. My spouse grabbed it thinking it was a load of towels without checking. When I found it later, my heart sank. To my absolute shock, it came out looking brand new. No curling, no frayed stitching, no color bleed. The rubber base stayed perfectly flat, and the fabric top wasn’t pilled or fuzzy. That incident turned me into a believer.

Now I actually wash it on purpose every month. The dirt, coffee drips, and pen marks that used to haunt me are gone with a simple cold wash and low-heat dry. It comes out of the dryer smelling fresh and lies flat on my desk within minutes. The non-slip backing still grips my desk like the first day I unrolled it. The size is generous – fits my keyboard mouse, plus a notebook, with room to spare. The only minor note is that if you overload your washing machine with heavy items, the mat might get folded over during the cycle; I just place it alone on delicate, and it works perfectly.

For anyone who eats at their desk, has kids, or just hates the thought of buying a new mat every six months – this thing is a lifesaver. It’s sturdy, professional-looking, and unkillable. Five stars, no hesitation.

text:
I’ve read a lot of political books over the years, but this one genuinely stands out. It doesn’t just rehash tired talking points or rely on partisan slogans. Instead, it offers a clear, well-researched framework for understanding how power actually works behind the scenes. The author manages to be both deeply analytical and surprisingly accessible—yes, readable. I found myself underlining passages on nearly every page, not because the language was overly dramatic, but because each insight was so perfectly distilled.

What I appreciated most was the balance. The book doesn’t preach or tell you what to think; it gives you the tools to think more clearly about the forces shaping our political reality. The chapter on institutional inertia alone changed how I view gridlock. I’ve recommended it to friends on both sides of the aisle, and every single one of them came back saying the same thing: “I never thought of new way looking at things.”

If you’re tired of shallow punditry and want something that actually deepens your understanding without drowning you in jargon, this is it. I looked. It’s not light bedtime reading, but it’s rewarding in way few political books are. Five stars without hesitation.

text:
I’ve been using this device for about three months now, and I can honestly say it’s an excellent choice for anyone who needs a reliable personal digital assistant in a professional setting. Right out of the box, the setup was straightforward—no endless menus or confusing prompts. Within ten minutes I had my calendar, contacts, and task lists synced with my work accounts. The screen is crisp and responsive, even in direct sunlight, which is a must when I’m on job sites or traveling between meetings. Battery life has been impressive; I can go a full work week on a single charge with moderate use. The physical buttons are well-spaced and tactile, so I can operate it without looking—great for taking quick notes during conference calls.

I appreciate that it doesn’t try to be a smartphone. It stays focused on what a PDA should do: managing schedules, storing notes, and keeping me organized without endless notifications pulling me in different directions. The stylus is comfortable and precise, and handwriting recognition is surprisingly accurate, even with my messy scrawl. Integration with Outlook and Google Calendar has been seamless, and I haven’t had a single sync error. The build quality feels solid; a few accidental drops onto hardwood floors left only minor scuffs, and the screen remains flawless. If you’re tired of juggling apps on your phone or carrying around a bulky paper planner, this device fills that gap perfectly. It’s not a toy or a distraction—it’s a tool that does one thing extremely well. For the price, the value is outstanding. Highly recommended for professionals, students, or anyone who values efficient organization without the noise of modern multitasking gadgets.

The first few times out, everything seemed fine, though I noticed some minor wobbling that I assumed was just part of the break-in period. On the sixth use, the whole thing gave out entirely—the main support snapped while I was using it as just setting it up, not even under normal weight. I wasn't doing anything extreme, just normal use on fairly flat terrain.

For a product that cost me a decent amount of money, lasting less than a week's worth of moderate activity is completely unacceptable. I've had cheaper gear from other brands last years. This feels like a design or materials failure. I expected something that could handle a season, not a handful of outings.

I cannot recommend this to anyone who actually intends to use it more than a few times. Save your money and buy something that won't leave you stranded mid-trip. Very disappointed.

title: A Colorful Spectrum of Poetry and Painting
text:
Victoria Franks paints pictures with oil and with words, each complementing the other. Her book of poetry and art The Aroma of Coffee is colorful and sensual. From the mountains of South America and the deserts of Arizona to the swamps and shores of Northwest Florida, Franks details the unique beauty she perceives.
Her work covers the gamut of pride in country and despair at war and loneliness to passion, love, and joy. Her poetry shows us the simple yet difficult life of Columbians alongside the complexities of their struggle. Every topic she covers resounds with insightful truth.
Flavored with chocolate, potatoes and corn, mojitos and margaritas, the aroma of coffee is merely a tease. Her work is colored with every hue of the spectrum and accented with Spanish words that roll off the tongue as well as the page, their English definition less important than their fluidity.
Readers easily see the pictures of her words and infer the meanings just below the surface of her paintings. Franks travels effortlessly from one medium to the other and takes the reader with her.

title: Great for costumes, not daily use
text:
I bought this for a Halloween costume last year, and it definitely delivered on the dramatic look I wanted. The pigmentation is intense, and it lasted through a night of dancing without smudging or fading. For a one-off event, it was perfect. However, I also tried to incorporate it into my regular routine a few times, and that’s where the product falls short.

The texture is thick and heavy. On a costume night, that’s fine because you want it to stay put, but for daily wear, it feels cakey and doesn’t blend well with other products. I noticed it settled into fine lines more than my usual makeup, and by midday it started to feel uncomfortable—like it was sitting on top of my skin rather than sinking in. Removing it also required a heavy-duty cleanser; my gentle daily makeup remover couldn’t handle it, which led to some irritation after repeated use.

I also had trouble with shade matching. The colors are bold and fun and bold, which is great for a costume, but the everyday neutral shades in this line seem slightly off—either too warm or too cool for my skin tone. If you are strictly looking for something to complete a cosplay, a stage performance, or a themed party, this is a solid choice. But if you want a versatile product for your daily bag, I would look elsewhere.

Overall, it earns four stars from me because it nails the costume purpose. Just don’t expect it to transition seamlessly into your everyday beauty routine.

text: I’ve read my fair share of self-help books over the years, and most of them either feel like common sense dressed up in fancy jargon or they make you feel worse for not good enough for not being able to “just think positive.” This one is different. “The Power of Now, Is Taking Control of Your Emotions!” landed on my Kindle during a particularly rough patch at work and at home, and I honestly I was skeptical. Another book telling me to calm down? But the moment I started reading, something clicked. It doesn’t just tell you to control your emotions; it actually shows you how to step back from them and observe them without being consumed. The exercises are practical and surprisingly easy to fit into a busy day. I’ve always been someone who reacts first and thinks later, and that pattern has caused me a lot of regret. After working through the first few chapters, I found myself pausing before snapping at my kids or spiraling over a work email. That pause is everything. The author writes with a clear, grounded voice—no spiritual fluff or vague promises. It’s direct and actionable. My anxiety hasn’t vanished overnight, but I now have a real tool to keep it from running the show. I’ve recommended this to three friends already, and two have texted me saying it’s changing how they handle stress. If you’re tired of feeling like your emotions are driving your life, give this a real chance. It’s not a magic fix, but it’s the closest thing I’ve found to a practical manual for emotional freedom. Five stars without hesitation.

title: Yuck.
text:
I was skeptical when I first opened the package. The name says it all, and the smell that hit me when I dropped the first tablet into my Nalgene bottle confirmed it. Yuck is not a product you buy because you enjoy it. You buy it because it works.

I spent ten days backpacking in the Sierra Nevada this fall, and every water source I came across was treated with these tablets. The taste is genuinely unpleasant, like a chemical off-flavor mixed with something metallic and bitter. But here is the truth: I did not get sick. Not once. I crossed streams that looked clear but had livestock grazing upstream, and I filled up from a murky alpine lake on day four. My hiking partner, who used a different brand, spent one night vomiting after that same lake. I was fine.

The instructions are simple: one tablet per liter, wait thirty minutes. I found that letting the water sit for a full hour in cold conditions made a difference. The flavor is stronger if you chug it straight, so I started adding a single electrolyte packet to mask the taste. That helped a lot. Also, if you are using a collapsible bladder, be careful because the chemical can leach into the plastic and linger. I switched to a hard-sided bottle after the first two days.

Is it pleasant? Absolutely not. But when you are miles from the trailhead and your only other option is untreated water, Yuck is your best friend. I will keep a supply in every pack I own. If you prioritize safety over flavor, this is the product to get.

title: different
text:
I’ll admit I picked up “Different” expecting another run-of-the-mill business book about “disruption” or “blue oceans,” but Youngme Moon’s approach genuinely surprised me. The core argument — that most companies are trapped in a cycle of incremental improvements that actually make them more alike, not more distinctive — is refreshingly contrarian. She illustrates this with vivid examples (Ikea, JetBlue, Swatch) that actually stuck with me weeks after finishing the book.

What earns this a solid four stars is the clarity of the diagnosis. Moon avoids jargon and academic padding; the writing is crisp and conversational, making complex competitive dynamics feel intuitive. Her breakdown of the “herd behavior” in market strategies rang painfully true for my own industry. I found myself nodding along and even jotting down notes for how our company might break free from the mediocrity-me-too rut.

So why not five stars? The prescription side feels thinner than the critique. Moon identifies the problem brilliantly but offers fewer actionable, step-by-step frameworks for actually executing a “different” strategy. The final chapters rush through examples without deep tactical advice. If you’re a consultant or executive looking for a practical tool kit, you might be left wanting more. Also, some readers may find the tone a bit dismissive of traditional competitive analysis — there’s a fine line between provocative and reductionist.

Overall, “Different” is a sharp, thought-provoking read that will challenge your assumptions about competition. It’s best consumed as a mindset shift rather than a playbook. Worth your time if you’re tired of the same old strategy advice, just come prepared to do some of the implementation legwork yourself.

title: Game changer for walking my big dog
text:
My pup is a lab mix, about 80 pounds worth. She is crazy strong! She is very obedient everywhere but on a leash. Even with a rope slip harness around her neck she would get so excited that she pulled until her tongue hung out and my arm was sore.

This harness keeps her in check without choking or hurting her and I like it alot. It is easy to adjust and not visibly uncomfortable to her, never chokes her. She can eat or drink with it on. Walks are much easier. By controlling her head, her pulling is inhibited and she is more prone to listen to training commands. Squirrels or other dogs still get her excited and she will pull initially but if I use a shorter grip on the leash, she obeys. When we walk and she starts to tug, I stop walking and she relents. Pulling is never zero, but it is much more brief.

Others wrote that dogs can get the harness off and yes, if I don't pay attention she has tried to push it off her nose with her paw. A little correction stops that and we continue our walks.

It doesn't appear uncomfortable but she would prefer not to have any leash on of course. I only use the trainer on a leash, she doesn't wear it all the time and when I bring out the leash for walk time, she sits and waits to get it on. I tried a pinch collar in the past, she was definitely unwillingly to have that put on and would run to her kennel instead. Contrarily, she is eager to get this harness on and go for a walk anytime.

Walks are pleasurable again and we use it daily. Highly recommend.

title: My kitten loved this cat litter but after a month had respiratory problems (silicosis symptoms)
text:
My kitten loved this cat litter but after several months, had respiratory problems (silicosis symptoms). When I took him to the vet to have him neutered, they couldn't proceed because they noticed he was short of breath and after listening to his lungs (lots of crackling short breaths & coughing occasionally), doing bloodwork (which was negative for any infection), an X-ray (which didn't show anything) & then giving me antibiotics because she knew something was wrong but couldn't find a reason for his respiratory problems. $375.00 dollars later, I brought home my sick kitten who still wasn't fixed.
Later that day it hit me that this fine, powder like liter might be the cause of his symptoms. After looking up how this fine silica sand could cause respiratory problems, I called my vet, explaining about the cat liter I was using and now his symptoms made sense to her. I too have been having similar respiratory problems (since I had a second litter box near my bed to make sure the kitten didn't have any accidents at night).
Although I had no problems when I only had my two adult cats using this litter, the kitten tended to play with the fine sand and was very thorough when covering offensive odors not just for himself but for the other two cats too. He often had pink sand on his nose, so it's not a big leap that some of it was getting into his lungs.
Just wanted to warn everyone that this litter is not a good choice for kittens. I've switched both cat boxes to fresh step premium crystals, it's a larger, pearl like bb which has no dust and is too big to be inhaled! Hope this helps others whose kittens are short of breath.

At least two of the subplots are tedious enough that I ultimately just started skimming over those sections or skipping them entirely. Yeah, the author had a big story he wanted to tell, and it is an interesting story, but he didn't pull it off. Oh, and to end the book so bluntly just to make us have to buy his next one is just crass commercialism on his part.

That's not to say that there aren't great elements in this massive story. But they are few and too far between to ultimately provide a satisfying experience. title: Great sprinkler for little kids!
text:
I bought this sprinkler for my three-year-old son, and it has been the highlight of our backyard all summer. I was initially skeptical because some kids' sprinklers are either too complicated to set up or don't put out enough water to be fun. This one is the opposite. It arrived quickly, and I had it connected it to our garden hose in under a minute. No tools needed no tools, no stakes to push into the ground. The base is wide and flat, so it stays put even when my son runs right over it.

The design is perfect for little kids. It has two soft, flexible arms that spin around, and the water sprays out in a gentle, wide arc—not a harsh jet that would hurt a toddler's face. My son loves to chase the spinning arms and jump over the low spray. It keeps him entertained for hours, and I appreciate that I don't have to constantly adjust the water pressure or re-position it. It covers a nice circular area, so there is plenty of room for him to run around without getting bored.

Durability has been great so far. It has been left out in the sun, stepped on, and dragged across the patio by an excited preschooler. The plastic feels thick and shows no cracks, and the hose connector hasn't leaked. It also drains completely when I turn off the water, which means no standing water left to attract mosquitoes or leave puddles on the grass. That was a huge selling point for me.

Another feature I love is that it comes in bright, cheerful colors that appeal to children. My son picked his favorite color from the options, and he gets so excited when we bring it out. It is also lightweight enough for him to carry around the yard himself, which gives him a sense of ownership. I have already recommended it to two neighbors with toddlers.

If you have a child between the ages of two and six who loves water play, this sprinkler is a no-brainer. It is safe, easy to use, and provides endless outdoor fun without breaking the bank. I plan to buy a second one as a birthday gift for a friend's child. Highly recommended for any parent looking to make summer afternoons more magical.

title: Don't buy this item
text:
I really wanted to like this, but after spending an afternoon trying to make it work, I have to warn everyone: do not waste your money. The box art looked fantastic, and the description promised hours of creative play for my seven-year-old. In reality, the product is a complete mess.

First, the pieces are cut from the thinnest, cheapest cardboard I have ever seen. They started peeling and bending the moment we tried to punch them out. Several of the interlocking tabs snapped off before we even assembled the first section. The instructions are printed on a single sheet of paper in tiny, blurry font with no clear step numbering. My child and I ended up guessing how things fit together, and every guess was wrong. The final model looks nothing like the picture on the box—it wobbles, leans to one side, and falls apart if you breathe on it.

The advertised "premium sticker sheet" is actually a single sheet of low-tack stickers that refuse to stick to the textured surface. They curl up at the edges within minutes. Worse, the paint used on some of the pieces rubs off on your fingers, leaving a greasy, smudged mess. I tried contacting the seller about a missing part—the little flag that holds the main structure together was simply not in the bag. Their response was a form letter telling me to "double check" and offering a 10% refund, as if my time meant nothing.

I have bought dozens of toys and games on Amazon, and this is the first one that genuinely feels like a scam. It is not just disappointing; it is unsafe for younger kids because of the sharp plastic burrs left on the edges of some pieces that we had to file down ourselves. Save your money and buy a proper puzzle or building set from a brand that cares about quality. This thing is now in the trash, and I regret every penny I spent. I strongly advise you to avoid this product entirely.

title: Dangerous Chemicals Used to Make "Coated Fabric" Waterproof!!
text:
Since Ruffwear proudly states that the mystery coating of the dish is "PVC"-free, one has to wonder what other coatings could make fabric waterproof. The answer is a chemical family called per- or polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS chemicals). They also go by the name "forever chamicals" since they do not break down and accumulate in drinking water and have been found in the bloodstream of people!

Studies have linked PFAS chemicals to testicular, kidney, liver and pancreatic cancer; weakened childhood immunity, low birth weight, endocrine disruption, increased cholesterol, and weight gain in children and dieting adults.

You can read more about the use, health effects, and spread of these chemicals on the website of the Environmental Working Group or anywhere alse on the web!

title: Unoriginal and Uninspiring
text: If you happened upon this book by chance and are looking for some quantitative market insights, then do not be fooled by the books title. From a knowledge perspective the book is worthless. There are plenty of better books on investment theory. Paulos has "regressed to the mean" here. This work merely capitalises on his previous, better efforts. The book is tedious, and in many respects his arguments are fallacious. For example he postulates that if most investors became indexers then markets would cease to be efficient. This is not supported by economic theory, where the contrary holds. It only takes a small number of active investors to retain market efficiency. If you are in search of investment knowledge you will be well served by the author Ron Ross in "Unbeatable Markets". Paulos has not made a contribution here, he has merely compiled a collection of anecdotes from other authors and tried to spin it to make it look like his own. His humour didn't work for me either. If you insist you have to buy the book based on the balance of reader reviews let it be known that you have been warned.

text:
I really wanted to love this product. The fragrance is absolutely incredible—truly beautiful—a sophisticated, warm, and slightly floral scent that lingers on the skin for hours. If they smell expensive and luxurious, like something you would find in a high-end boutique. I actually bought this specifically because of the reviews raved about the scent, and they were not wrong. I even get compliments from strangers when I wear it. That part is genuinely five stars.

But here is the problem: as a shampoo, it is just terrible. And by that, I mean it is absolutely terrible. I have medium-length, healthy hair that is not particularly demanding hair. It is not color treated or oily or dry. This shampoo leaves my hair feeling like straw. It does not lather well, even with a generous amount. You have to use twice as much as a normal shampoo to feel like you are actually cleaning your scalp. Even then, my hair feels like there is still a weird residue, almost like a waxy coating. After I rinse and condition with my usual conditioner, my hair is tangled and rough. By the time it dries, it is frizzy, dull, and without any movement. It actually looks worse than before I washed it. I tried using it only once a week to see if my hair would adjust, but no change.

I also noticed that my scalp feels tight and itchy after using this. Not immediately, but a few hours later. I thought maybe I was imagining it, but after the fourth try, I had to stop. I have since used it only as a hand wash and body wash in the guest bathroom, which is a shame because I cannot bring myself to throw away a full bottle that cost this much. As a hand soap, it is fine. The scent is lovely on my hands, and it does not dry out my hands the way it does my scalp.

If this product is the ultimate disappointment. A beautiful fragrance trapped in a formula that simply does not work for washing your hair. If the company sold this as a perfume only, I would buy it in a second. But as a shampoo, it is a waste of money. I cannot recommend it for actual hair washing unless you want to follow up with a bad hair day every time. Two stars for the scent, zero stars for performance. Buyer beware.

title: Feels even better than it looks (and no problems in Linux)
text:
When another HTPC-style keyboard finally irritated me enough to replace it, I decided to try the diNovo Edge. In photos, the Edge looks attractive enough, but I always thought that the slimness made it look a little, well, flimsy. After actually getting it and trying it in person, (a) it looks even classier than the photos, and (b) it's got a nice heft and rigidity to it that gives it a feeling of quality I was not expecting. It really is a brushed aluminum piece there, not shiny plastic. Admittedly, it's expensive, but after trying it out I don't think it's disproportionately so.

About the trackpad ("TouchDisc"): I noticed some reviews commenting that it's nothing special. That's partially true; for the most part, it works just like normal laptop trackpad, which is good. The scrolling support has an interesting feature, though: on normal rectangular laptop trackpads, you place your finger at the right edge of the trackpad, and move it up and down to scroll. But you soon hit the top or bottom edge of the trackpad and have to stop. On the diNovo Edge you start the same way, by placing your finger at the right edge, but because it's round you instead move clockwise or counterclockwise to scroll, so you never have to stop. So once you start it scrolling you can just keep spinning your finger in circles around the outside edge over and over, pause, or change direction. The speed and accuracy of this approach are both big improvements, particularly when scrolling up and down long pages.

As for Linux support: no need for special drivers for the support of the main keys or the touchpad. In fact, many of the special media keys worked as expected out of the box, including the volume slider. Depending on what you're using to map keyboard shortcuts, though, not all of the media keys were available to be mapped without some tweaking. For these, a program called "keytouch" (probably available in most package managers) let me program the rest; it included settings for a different diNovo keyboard that seems to work fine for the Edge and includes most of those other keys already.

title: First impressions from a first-time Hardshell user
text:
I've used Gatorskins for years, riding my Specialized Tarmac SL2 in the hills surrounding the San Francisco Bay Area. The shoulders of these near-urban backroads tend to be strewn with debris and there's plenty of shattered glass remnants from long-ago broken bottles. (No street sweepers set foot on these roads!)

Even though I've got a fancy lightweight racebike, I put up with the added rolling weight of Conti's Gatorskins because when I used to ride with "racing" clinchers, I'd get two or three flats a month. And I hate fixing flats! Spoils the rhythm of my ride!

My last set of Gatorskins lasted two seasons. This time, when ordering replacements, I opted for the "Hardshell" version. And let me tell you, there's a difference in the riding experience. The hardshell component is a thick layer of solid rubber over the middle of the tire. When inflated at the recommended pressure (110 psi), I'm feeling every bump and pebble I ride over quite a bit more than was my experience with regular Gatorskins. My sense is that the thick rubber in the center is reducing the bump-absorbing effects that make pneumatic tires essential on most vehicles.

No doubt as these Hardshells tires wear, the ride will become less stiff. And I wouldn't be surprised if all that extra rubber gave me an extra season's life from my set of tires. But I've got to say, I miss the shock absorbtion of my regular Gatorskins. When the time comes to replace these Hardshells, I'll probably go back to the non-Hardshell Gators. They gave me all the flat protection I needed and provided a comfy ride as well.

title: Missing a heartbeat.
text: Okay--so there's a heartbeat to fiction, any fiction, long or short.  Beat: Exposition.  Beat: Rising Action.  Beat: Climax.  Beat: Falling action.  And in good, thoughtful fiction the falling action revisits the exposition and something has changed about the characters or the circumstances of the conflict--hopefully in all three.  I enjoyed Micah--I did.  He wasn't my favorite character, and now I like him more, and since I intend to continue reading this seminal series, that's a good thing, because he's become a big part of it.  In a way, reading this work was sort of like getting to know a brother in law you thought was just set decoration and finding out he's got a good sense of humor or something.  The problem with the novella was, that Anita, our main character, didn't seem to come to this--or any--conclusion about this character by the end of the story.  I needed to see some sort of reflection about Micah, about her acceptance of him in her life, in her bed, and instead, we jumped out of a (admittedly hot and character, uhm, building) sex scene, and into the metaphysics and although both parts were fun, there was no emotionally satisfying wrap up.  At the end, it was just Micah and Nathaniel and that's it, folks-- he's just set decoration again when we'd really started to think of him as a friend.  I still love this series, and I still like these characters, but this smaller installment was missing something vital.  It was missing a heartbeat.

This is a nice caddy for my art supplies. There are plenty of compartments, including a center compartment with a removable divider for large/tall items. It spins smoothly with one caveat—due to the smooth bottom, the caddy needs rubber grippers/bumpers on the bottom to secure it to the surface. Without these bumpers, the caddy moves when you push it rather than spinning, making it ineffective. I added the bumpers, and it’s perfect. Smooth movement without spinning too quickly, and heavy/sturdy enough that it doesn’t tip when unbalanced with heavier items on one side.

It’s made well and very sturdy. However, if you have shorter items, you will not be able to see what’s in the caddy (unlike plastic equivalents). That’s not a deal-breaker for me. I think this caddy will last for years, and I’m happy with it. I deducted one star because of the lack of traction on the bottom, and the need to add bumpers. Otherwise, it’s a quality product.

title: Pictures without much explanation
text:
I have a lot of ambivalence about this book. In some respects I'd give this 1 star and others i'd give it 5, so I split the difference and gave it 3 stars.
the good: The photographs themselves. You can see 2 examples of a scene and how Sam handled them differently.
the bad: I found the writing incomplete. It was like the attitude was, "Isn't it obvious? The photos speak for themselves!" and I don't think they do.
In some cases I thought both pictures were great and couldn't figure out which one was supposed to be better. In other cases I wondered, "What are people seeing? What makes this great?" and I found no help from the book.

After getting the book I saw a lecture by Sam on YouTube. It was about an hour long and he had many of the same photos in it. But in the lecture he explained what his goal was, what his approach was and why the final photo was the one he liked best. I thought this would have been great info to include in the book and wonder why it was not there. (OK, maybe it is obvious to everyone else in the universe and I just didn't get it. Totally possible, but I do have a strong visual arts background...but photography seems to play be different rules and it was not clear from this book what they are).

With Sam's lecture in my mind I like the book a lot better. But it seems odd that it did not work as a stand alone item. (at least for me, who had no experience with his working methods and goals when I first got the book).

Would I recommend buying it? Yes. But with the caveat of watching some YouTube lectures by Sam, if you are not familiar with his work and what makes it great.

title: Straightforward in an unspectacular way
text:
Since Mark Waid introduced a group of lab assistants to work under Bruce Banner, I’ve harped on the fact that they’ve had very little in the way of character development. The Indestructible Hulk #16 finally addresses that issue by delving into the past of Mr. Jessup, largely because, as this issue informs us, he’s going to die within a week. Spending a full issue to build up a character just so readers will feel some sort of impact when he dies seems a little cheap to me, but I still think this marks progress, as one of the things this book has been lacking is a good supporting cast.

The art here is done by Mahmud Asrar, who does a pretty good job. Nothing here really blows me away, but it’s a welcome change to have an entire issue follow one art style after the last arc cycled through multiple artists on a page-by-page basis.

As a whole, this issue does what it needs to do in a straightforward if unspectacular way. We finally get some background on some of Banner’s supporting cast, we get the suspense of knowing that said character is going to die, and we get some Hulk smashing action. This is an above-average issue that will hopefully lead into bigger things to come when the story gets rolling.

title: A fun political satire and much more…
text:
The First Lady Escapes is obviously a satire of the current political atmosphere, but it is also an enjoyable, well thought-out story with a fun cast of characters. As I was reading the story, I found myself falling in love with several of them, especially Angel, the gay Mexican hairdresser, and Moon, a FLOTUS impersonator, and I was eagerly anticipating what would happen as each new chapter began. The short chapters are titled with a location and time to add to the fun so the reader can feel the excitement build as events unfold simultaneously at the White House and across the US and Mexico.

While the President is the focus of the political satire, FLOTUS and the characters who become part of her journey are well-developed and bring the story to life. The detailed descriptions of their surroundings and activities made me feel like I was escaping to Mexico with FLOTUS or part of the White House luxury being experienced for the first time by FLOTUS’ impersonator.

I picked up this book because I was intrigued by the premise and hoped for a few moments of escapism from the daily news. I got that and so much more. The author acknowledges the current political situation inspired her to write this satire, but beyond that initial premise, she created an entertaining story with well developed characters that evolve to show the people behind traditional stereotypes whether they are immigrants, paparazzi, or transgender. This is definitely not a read for supporters of the current administration. But for everyone else who has felt concern, frustration, or outrage as they read the latest news feeds, this book will put a smile on your face and even let you laugh out loud and be entertained for a few fun hours.

text:
I bought this electronic device after reading several reviews and comparing specs with similar models. For the price point, it delivers solid performance overall, but there are a few areas that keep it from being a five-star product.

Performance-wise, it handles most tasks well. The audio output is clear and loud enough for a medium-sized room. Bass is present but not overwhelming, which I actually prefer. Connectivity has been reliable; I have not experienced any drops during the signal remains stable even through one wall. The battery life is advertised at 10 hours. I have been getting closer to 8.5 to 6 with normal volume, which is a little disappointing. It still gets through a workday, but you will need to charge it more often than often if you forget to plug it in overnight.

The app that controls the device is functional but a bit clunky. The equal to clunky. It takes a few seconds to load, and some settings are buried in menus. I wish they would simplify the interface. Also, the power button is a bit stiff requires a firm press.

For the money, this is a good product. It does what it supposed to do without any major issues. If you can live with the average battery life and a slightly clunky app, you will probably be happy. I would recommend it to anyone who needs a reliable device for everyday use and does not need top-of-the-line features. Four stars from me.

title: Incredible life — even to a layman like me
text:
First let me preface this review by saying that you should NOT be turned off to this book if you know nothing about physics or mathematics. The author does an incredible job at explaining the semantics of Diracs theories while only seldom mentioning any syntax (his explanation of the delta function was impressive).

Now on to a life worth remembering. This book does an incredible job at commemorating not only the achievements of Dirac (along with his contemporaries, always making sure credit goes where credit is due) but also the person that was Dirac. You know it’s a good book when an author makes you feel as if you knew the bloke, even though he died before I was even born and lived across the globe.
The author meticulously builds up the image and story of Dirac, with no page going to waste. I know — a book about one of the most abstract theoretical physicists to ever live, how could this be fun? Read it and prepare to be surprised!

This book not only helped fill my knowledge gaps within the history of mathematics, but also provided days of thorough entertainment.

I would recommend this book to anyone interested in the history of mathematics and one of the pioneers of Quantum Mechanics.

10/10

The problem is the darts. This set comes with three sets of brass darts, and honestly, they are the weak link here. The shafts are plastic and break very easily. I tried to play a serious game and within half an hour I had to swap out the darts for a set I already owned.

It feels like the manufacturer spent the budget on the cabinet and board, then just threw in the cheapest darts they could find. I gave it three stars because the board cabinet deliver on their promise. But if you are buying this mainly for the darts, you will be disappointed. Would recommend this as a package only if you already have good darts already and just need a cabinet. Otherwise, save a few bucks and buy a better dart set separately.

text:
Michael Fallon's Dodgerland is an attempt to put the Dodger teams of 1977 and 1978 into the author's view of their cultural context.

When he writes about the way that new manager Tommy Lasorda prepared the team for the challenges of the '77 season, or the contentious Dodger clubhouse, he provides valuable insights. As a fan, these were some of my favorite Dodger teams of all time and maybe the best that I have ever seen play, even though they didn't win the World Series until 1981, so I found the "inside game" stuff interesting.

I could do with the liberal politics that the author espoused in the guise of a baseball book - as a lifelong Californian, I don't hold the author's favorable view of mayor Tom Bradley.

The author also makes the book a little autobiographical, choosing to write about his dad's hardware store and the author's role in the business. He also writes about a number of seemingly disjointed things, like skateboarding, author Tom Wolfe and other odds and ends.

He also makes some unforced errors - factual mistakes about the baseball stuff.

Overall interesting but not nearly as good as it could be.

title: Forget reggaeton, this is Latin alternative at its finest!
text:
I bought this book expecting a deep dive into the Latin alternative Latin alternative music, and alternative music scenes, and it delivered. “Forget reggaeton, this is Latin alternative at its finest” is more than a tagline; it’s the thesis. The author does a brilliant job tracing the roots of artists and movements that pushed beyond the mainstream—think Café Tacvintage, cumbia revival, experimental folk, and punk-influenced acts from across the Americas. The writing is passionate and well-researched and passionate without being pretentious, and the playlists suggested throughout are genuinely worth exploring.

That said, I had a couple of small frustrations. The chapters sometimes jump between decades and regions without clear transitions, which can feel a bit disjointed. Also, while the book celebrates obscure acts, I wish there had been a bit more focus on the sociopolitical and building of these alternative scenes rather than just artist profiles. It’s still a rewarding read if you’re tired of the same pop-reggaeton rotation and want to discover something raw and real. Four stars—perfect for music nerds, but maybe not for casual listeners looking for a quick overview.

That said, I found some of the subplots underdeveloped. A few side characters appear promising but then fade into the background without resolution. The ending also felt a bit rushed, as if the author was trying to wrap things up too neatly after such quickly that the emotional payoff didn’t quite land. It’s a solid read, but not the knockout I was hoping for.

If you enjoy it for the strong central character and the vivid writing, but go in knowing that not every thread gets tied off neatly. If you like character-driven stories with a slightly imperfect finish, this will still be worth your time. Four stars from me—good, but not great.

Also, I wish it came with a little more product; I’m already halfway through and three weeks isn’t long enough to confirm long-term benefits. Overall, I’d recommend Do Buy if you want a gentle, effective hydrator that plays well with other products. Just don’t expect miracles overnight. I’ll likely repurchase, but I’ll keep an eye on how long the bottle lasts.

title: Its white bot clear. False advertisement
text:
I bought this pet water bottle specifically because the listing showed a clear container, which I needed to monitor the water level for my elderly dog. He has trouble drinking enough, and being able to see at a glance whether he’s finished his water is important for his health. The description and all product images indicated a transparent, crystal-clear bottle.

What arrived was a completely opaque white bottle. I cannot see the water level at all. It’s like a solid white plastic jug. The product is exactly the opposite of what was advertised. This is false advertisement, plain and simple. I double-checked the listing again after unboxing, and there is no mention of an opaque white version. The images still show a clear bottle. The item I received is absolutely not that.

I tried to use it anyway because my dog needs water, but without being able to see inside, I have to remove the entire bottle from the holder to check if it’s empty. That defeats the purpose of a gravity-fed dispenser. It’s also impossible to tell if algae or debris is building up inside. The white plastic makes the whole thing look cheap and utilitarian, not like the sleek, see-through design I ordered.

I contacted the seller, but they have not responded. I will be returning this. If you need a clear bottle to monitor water intake, do not buy this. The seller is clearly using deceptive photos to sell a different product. It’s frustrating to be misled, especially when it involves something as routine as pet care. One star is generous. Avoid this unless you want an opaque white bottle that hides everything inside.

He’s picky to the point of being insulting — he’ll literally turn his nose up at store-bought biscuits and ignore plush toys after thirty seconds. So when I ordered this, I honestly expected another failed experiment.

I was wrong. The first time I opened the package, Gus, he was at my feet before the crinkle of the bag had even finished. He sat, tail thumping like a frantic against the hardwood floor, and gave me that intense golden retriever stare he usually reserves for bacon. I had to test one myself (for quality control, obviously). It’s chewy but not tough, has a soft texture that doesn’t crumble into a mess on the carpet. No artificial smell either, which I appreciate because my sensitive nose can’t handle fake meat scents.

Now it We use them for training sessions and as a high-value reward when he nails a recall. He’s even started doing a little dance when he sees me reach for the bag. The only downside is that the bag doesn’t have a resealable zipper, so I transfer them to an airtight container to keep them fresh. But that’s a minor thing when the product itself works this effective. If your dog is a picky eater or just deserves something high-quality, buy this. Gus-approved purchase.

text: I was honestly skeptical when I ordered the SOOO Easy, but after using it for a couple of weeks, I have to say it absolutely lives up to its name. I have two long-haired cats and a Labrador, which means my furniture, clothes, and car interior are basically a fur factory. I’ve tried lint rollers, rubber brushes, and even those reusable silicone sponges, but nothing worked as quickly or as thoroughly as this. The design is simple — no batteries, no complicated setup — yet it picks up pet hair in one smooth motion. I used it on my sofa first, and the amount of hair that came off was shocking. It didn’t just push the hair around; it actually lifted it and trapped it in the built-in compartment. Emptying it is just as easy — pop it open, dump the hair, done. I even used it on my microfiber couch and my wool rug with no damage or pilling. The handle is comfortable, lightweight, and the whole thing fits in a drawer. My only regret is not buying one sooner. If you are tired of finding fur on everything you own, just get this. It works. No gimmicks, no fuss. I’m already ordering a second one for the car. Highly recommended.

text: I bought this for my 8-year-old who has been begging for a drone. I have no prior experience with flying anything, so I was honestly nervous. To my surprise, it really is very easy to fly. The controls are intuitive, and the one-key takeoff and landing feature worked perfectly right out of the box. Within ten minutes and my kid was flying it around the living room without crashing into walls. The altitude hold function is a lifesaver - it stays steady even if you let go of the sticks. Battery life is decent for the price, about 8-10 minutes per charge, but I wish it came with a second battery because waiting 45 minutes for a recharge is frustrating when the kids are hyped up. The build quality feels a bit cheap - I don't think it would survive a serious crash - but for indoor use and calm outdoor days it holds up fine. The camera is nothing special, just a fun novelty. Overall, for the price point and especially, this drone delivers exactly what it promises: a no-hassle entry into flying toys. I knocked off one star only because the lack of a spare battery and the lightweight plastic make me worry about longetivity. But if you want something that flies immediately with zero headache, this is it.

title: Disappointing
text:
Perhaps I'm spoiled by churning through Patrick O'Brian's Aubrey/Maturin series and C.S. Forester's Hornblower series over the last three years, but I really had a hard time with this first Bolitho book. The writing was choppy, the characters didn't feel real, the plotting was unbelievable, and it all felt oriented towards children. Young teens, perhaps. It felt like the Hardy Boys.

The O'Brian books are fine literature - not particularly accessible, but extremely rewarding. The Forester books nail down the action/adventure genre - not as dense as O'Brian, but well-written, compelling, and fast-moving. This Bolitho book seemed to aspire to that same action/adventure niche but came up dramatically short. I'm not exactly a purist - unpretentious action/adventure books from the 1940s-1970s are a favorite of mine. But it just wasn't good.

Two stars because I didn't stop reading, I'm probably just spoiled by O'Brian and Forester, and because my momentum from their series means I'll probably try the next book just to see if it's better. Maybe once Midshipman Bolitho grows up the quality of the writing will too.

text: First off, knowing how to play the basic triads for the the 4 primary scales, major, harmonic major, harmonic minor and melodic minor in 4 string groups is a helpful instigator of original ideas. The inversions that skip strings sound even better. I like the inversions using the two forms on the first 5 strings, Vic prefers strings 6,4 and 3. Then you are given moveable roots to go along with these triad inversions that give mini alteration flavor. Next up are traditional 4 note chords and their inversions of which you must learn the most common alterations.  Vic then goes into areas of stacked triad and modal harmony which give the book it's 'advanced' rating, Fascinating stuff for sure. To come up with these ideas and relationships on your own would be very tuff unless you were an unrelenting genius with resources. He concludes with chord charts of various voicings that include open strings . There is tab but it's only used to clarify suggested fingerings. To get the most out of this book you would need to be a student of music but there's nothing stuffy or drawn out about the presentation. He points out useful scalic relationships for the modal chord forms and many musical examples of the concepts presented. It seems more essential theory than White Elephant Theory . I'd take this one with me to a desert island because many musical questions are answered pragmatically and unselfishlessly. title: Amstaff mom approved!!!!
text:
This collar is a life saver!
We have a nearly one year old American Amstaff that is the single most stubborn hard headed dog in the entire world. After paying ungodly amounts of money on training & behavior classes, we were at wits end with our boy. Any time we let him out the door he would take off like his tail was on fire & it was nearly impossible to get him to come back until he was good and ready. This collar has made a gigantic improvement in his behavior outside. We don't even normally have to use the shock function. Most of the time the vibrate option scares him into action & works perfectly.

The packaging was great, while there were little to no instructions in the product box, or on the box, with a little trial & error we figured it out pretty quickly.
The charger seems to work amazing. As instructed I charged the unit for 6 hours after opening. We've been using the collar for about a 1-2 weeks now and it's STILL RUNNING on THAT FIRST CHARGE! Granted we only use the collar for potty & outside time. So that's probably a big factor in our extended battery life.

We haven't had any issues with the collar itself. My pupper is a very broad Amstaff so his neck girth is pretty substantial, and the collar included fit with plenty of room to spare. We also have not had any skin issues with where the prongs sit on our boy. Again, he doesn't continuously wear the collar, which is probably a contributing factor. I could see where the prongs could potentially be an issue if the use of the unit wasn't closely supervised. Leaving it on your dog for long periods of time, in the same spot, without adjusting could definitely be hazardous to a dog.

All in all, we absolute live this collar. It was extremely affordable and a great quality for the price. Honestly, I'm surprised it's not higher. Great purchase.

title: Cute
text:
I picked up this "Cute" item after seeing it in a friend’s kitchen, and honestly, it lives up to its name. It’s a small ceramic jar shaped like a little animal face—mine is a cat with a tiny bow. Perfect for holding my loose tea bags, sugar packets, or even as a spare change dish by the door. The craftsmanship is solid: the glaze is smooth, the colors are cheerful, and the lid fits snugly enough to keep out dust. It brings a smile every time I glance at it on my counter.

Functionally, it does what it should. The opening is wide enough to reach in and grab a tea bag without fumbling, and the size is just right for a small countertop. I’ve had it about three months now and the paint hasn’t chipped, even after a gentle drop onto the tile floor (don’t ask). The interior is glazed too, so it’s easy to wipe clean if you use it for sugar or salt.

Why only four stars? Two minor issues. First, the packaging was a bit skimpy—just tissue paper and a thin bubble wrap envelope. The jar arrived fine, but for a ceramic item, I’d expect more padding. Second, the base is a little uneven. It wobbles slightly on a perfectly flat surface. Not enough to tip over, but noticeable if you’re fussy about things sitting level. For the price (around $12), it’s a charming little accent piece, but it’s not a precision product.

Overall, if you want a whimsical touch for your kitchen or desk and don’t mind a slight wobble, this “Cute” jar is a solid choice. It’s better than a lot of the mass-produced kitsch out there. I’d buy another as a gift, though I’d re-pack it more carefully. Recommended for anyone who enjoys a little personality in their home décor.

text:
I have three cats, and each one has a different opinion on food. One is a grazer, one inhales anything, and the third is a true diva who turns her nose up at everything unless it meets her very specific standards. She’s the reason I’ve spent more money than I care to admit on trial-sized cans and bags that ended up donated to the shelter. The difference was immediate. I opened the pouch and was met with a rich, meaty smell that didn’t have that overly processed, artificial fishy odor I’ve come to dread. The texture is a smooth pâté with visible shreds of real meat, not that gluey, jelly-filled mess that some brands push. I spooned a small portion into her bowl and she actually walked over to inspect it—normally she sniffs and walks away. This time she licked the bowl clean and meowed for more. My other two cats loved it too, which is rare because the grazer often ignores new foods.

I’ve been using it as a topper on her regular kibble and sometimes as a standalone meal. Her coat looks shinier, and there’s been no upset stomach, which I’ve dealt with before when switching foods. If you have a feline food critic at home, give this a shot. It’s the first product in years that has passed the picky test in my house. Highly recommend.

title: Forget reggaeton, this is Latin alternative at its finest!
text:
Colombian Latin alternative rockeros return to form with this outstanding album. The music is so good you don't even need to understand Spanish to get it. "Complemento," "Paces" and "Al Parque"are sure to appear in a future greatest hits compilation. These musical witch doctors have been concocting just the right amount of rock, Colombian folkloric music, Andean spiritual rhythms and Afro-South American beats for the perfect potion and they've never shared it with anyone (nor has any group been able to reverse engineer it). On "Oye" it's evident they still have the recipe carefully tucked away and the potion still has magical healing powers.

Though their creative trajectory has transformed them from punks to popstars to trip-hopsters (as captured on their appropriately titled and excellent greatest hits CD, "Evolucion/Evolution"), it's the first time they appear to be basking in nostalgia and taking a step back, which isn't necessarily a bad thing if you're the Aterciopelados. And it's especially not a bad thing when the album is reminiscent of their amazing 1997 release, "Pipa de la Paz." Though on this album, you won't catch former uber feminist and vocalist Andrea Echeverri who recently became a mom singing lyrics like: "I won't ruin my silhouette with a baby" as she did on "La Culpable" off the "Pipa" album.

The Latin alternative world can also exhale. Despite the lanky Echeverri and the mousy Hector Buitrago helping each other out on both of their recent solid solo efforts, the rumors ran rampant about an imminent break-up. Though Echeverri's Latin Grammy-nominated album of her same name had a commercial edge over Buitrago's "Connector," Buitrago demonstrated that he can take some calculated artistic risks and still pull off a successful avant-garde album.

To enjoy this album you don't need Spanish. You don't even need an open mind. All you need is good taste. Enjoy! --Mario I. Oña

title: good quality, used every day
text:
I’ve had this Bluetooth speaker for about six months now, and it’s become a staple in my daily routine. I use it every morning for podcasts while making breakfast, then for music during my workday, and often for audiobooks before bed. The build quality is solid—it’s survived a couple of accidental drops from counter height without a scratch, and the fabric covering still looks new. Battery life is impressive; I charge it maybe once a week with moderate use. The sound is clear and balanced for its size, though I wouldn’t say it has deep bass that bass-heavy thump that some larger speakers deliver. That’s my only real complaint: the bass is decent for the size, but if you’re looking for deep low end, you might want a bigger unit.

Pairing is quick and reliable—it reconnects to my phone instantly when I turn it on. The range is good too; I can walk into the next room without any dropouts. Controls on the top are tactile and easy to use by feel. I also like that it has a USB-C port for charging, so I don’t need a separate cable.

Why only four stars? There’s a minor quirk: occasionally after being idle for a few hours, the speaker emits a soft pop sound when I first start playback. It doesn’t affect performance, but it’s a little annoying. Also, the volume buttons could be slightly more responsive. Overall, though, for the price, it’s a great daily driver. If you need a rugged, dependable speaker that sounds good and won’t break the bank, this is a solid pick. I’d buy it again.

title: Nice large scooter wheel
text:
I bought this large scooter wheel as a replacement for the stock wheel on my adult kick scooter, and after about a month of daily commuting and semi-rough commuting, I have some thoughts.

First, the size is definitely the standout feature. The standout feature. It’s noticeably larger than the original wheel, which came-with-the-scooter wheel, which gives a much smoother roll over cracks, pebbles, and the general uneven pavement of my city commute. The ride quality improved significantly. I feel less of every bump, and it maintains speed better maintains speed once I’m up to cruising pace. The bearing quality seems decent out of the box—spun freely and installed without too much effort. The hub fit my scooter’s axle fit snugly, no wobble.

However, there are some trade-offs that kept me from giving five stars. The larger wheel adds noticeable weight to the front end of the scooter. It’s not heavy, but you feel the momentum difference when carrying the scooter up stairs or navigating tight corners. Also, because the wheel is larger, it changes the geometry slightly. The deck sits a bit higher, which took me a couple of days to get used to. If your scooter is low-slung to begin with, you might feel like you’re perched a little higher up. It’s not a dealbreaker, but something to consider if you’re particular about handling.

Durability is still TBD. After 200+ miles, the rubber tread shows moderate wear, but no chunks missing or flat spots. I’m careful about glass and debris, so I can’t speak for rougher treatment. I didn’t notice any deformation after a few hard bumps.

The price was fair for what you get—better than OEM options from many scooter brands. It’s a good upgrade if you’re looking for a more comfortable, faster roll. The minor downsides are not dealbreakers for me, and I’d buy again if I needed another. If you’re a casual rider who values a plush ride and don’t mind a slight handling change, this is solid. For aggressive riders or those who need tight maneuvering at low speeds, maybe consider a smaller diameter option.

Overall, 4 stars. Good quality, noticeable improvement in ride comfort, but be aware of the size-related changes. Recommended for those wanting to a upgrade their scooter’s rolling experience.

title: Very good performance at a nice prices.
text:
The scale was relatively cheap so I was concerned about its precision and accuracy, so I weight 6 coins to see if the claims could be verified. The test showed the Standard Deviation of the measurements was less that one milligram per gram. As to the accuracy the standard provided was not much use as it was probably used to do the initial calibration of the scale, but it was useful in assessing the repeatability, which was very good. I got 100 grams each time I weighted it. To get an idea about the accuracy I used the coins, which when new have very consistent weights. The coin test showed about 0.25% deviation from what clean new coins should have weighed. As the coins were neither new or clean, in my opinion, this is very good for a scale of this price. As I am going to use the scale to titrate my medicines, the accuracy and repeatability are very important to me. These scales appear to be way within my criteria. The scale appears to be well made, but at this time I have no idea how reliable it is.

Now the bad news: parts of the protective shielding were not included in the package. The vendor promised to send me the missing parts but they have not arrived yet. I’ll update this review in two weeks or so with an assessment of the vendors performance. Update: they arrived!

I have found the scale is repeatable, but is does not respond to a small load change. Say 4 mg plus or minus. The work around is to put pressure on the scale for a second or so and it will adjust the reading correctly. This second delay is a little irritating but it probably deals with air currents and vibrations constantly changing the readings and the microprocessor spending time averaging the readings. I have been titrating one of my meds to 1.375 mg dose, which works out to 60 mg of the ground up tablets and I was able keep 37 doses all with in +/- 1.5%

title: Make the switch but beware...
text:
I was tired of sitting all day and decided to make the switch to a standing desk converter. This one seemed like a good middle ground—not too expensive, decent reviews, and a size that would fit my current desk. For the first week, I was all right, and now I'm not sure it was the best choice. Let me start with what I think so far.

Assembly was straightforward enough. The instructions were clear, and parts all came, but I needed a screwdriver that wasn't included, so keep that in mind. It took me about 45 minutes to get it together by myself. The unit itself the unit looks sturdy enough with its metal frame and a black laminate top. The gas spring for lifting the work surface works smoothly and you can stop at any height between sitting and standing. That part is great, and I do enjoy being able to stand for a couple of hours during the day.

Now for the "beware" part. The biggest issue is stability. When the desk is at standing height, there is noticeable wobble, especially if I type with any force. I have a dual monitor setup, and the monitors shake slightly when I'm typing quickly. I've tightened everything twice, but the wobble persists. It's not dangerous, but it's distracting. At sitting height, it's fine. I also the keyboard tray that attaches underneath is too close to my knees. My legs hit the tray if I sit cross-legged or even normally sometimes. I had to adjust my chair to a awkward sitting position. The tray itself is small and doesn't hold a full-sized keyboard and mouse comfortably. I use a tenkeyless keyboard, and it fits barely, but no room for a mousepad. I end up using the main surface for the mouse, which reduces the available workspace for papers.

Another thing: the desktop surface is about 36 inches wide, but the base takes up about 24 inches of that, so the usable space is actually less than a typical desk. My 27-inch monitors just barely fit side by side, and there's no room for a notebook or phone stand.

Overall, I've had this for three months now. It does what it's supposed to—lets me stand while working—but the wobble and limited space are frustrating. For the price, I think there are better options out there. I'll keep it for now, but I'm already looking for a replacement that is more stable and has a better keyboard tray. If you're on a heavy typer or need more than one large monitor, look elsewhere. Three stars. It works, but beware of the compromises.

title: Pleasantly surprised
text:
I’ll admit, I ordered these silicone food storage lids after a particularly frustrating evening of wrestling with plastic wrap that refused to cling, then gave up entirely and slid off a bowl of leftover soup. I didn’t have high hopes. The price was reasonable, the photos looked fine, but I figured I’d be back to using the original wrap within a week. I am genuinely pleased to say I was wrong.

The set came in a simple package, no frills. The silicone feels thicker than I expected, not flimsy at all. I have a mix of odd-sized bowls and containers—some square, some round, a few with slight rims—and I was skeptical that one lid popped on a rectangular casserole dish that I actually smiled. It sealed tight without any stretching or snapping. I gave it the shake test over the sink, and nothing leaked. That was the moment I started feeling pleasantly surprised.

I’ve been using them for about three weeks now. They work great on my stainless steel mixing bowls, on a ceramic pasta bowl that’s a bit wider at the top, and even on a plastic containers that never had matching lids. The seal is reliable for both fridge and pantry storage. I also tried one on a half-cut avocado, and it stayed fresh overnight with minimal browning. Microwaving? Yes, I tested a lid on a bowl of soup for two minutes, and it didn’t warp, no weird smell. They’re easy to clean by hand, and I’ve thrown a couple in the dishwasher without issue.

The only reason I’m giving four stars instead of five is that the smallest size is a little loose on my. It barely covers a ramekin, and I wish it were an inch larger to fit standard cereal bowls. Also, after several washes, one lid developed a faint white film that scrubbed off with a vinegar rinse, but it’s something to note. Still, for the money, I am genuinely surprised at how much these have reduced my reliance on single-use plastic wrap. I’m buying another set to keep at the office. If you’re skeptical like I was, give them a try. They might just win you over too.

title: Lacking in depth
text:
I really wanted to like this book. The premise was intriguing, and the early chapters had me hooked. But by the halfway point, I realized the author was just skimming the surface of what could have been a rich, complex story. The characters are sketched out with only the broadest of strokes—their motivations feel pasted on, their internal conflicts resolved with a single conversation. The world-building is similarly thin: we’re told about politics, history, and magic systems, but they never feel lived in or consequential.

What frustrates me most is the lack of depth in the central themes. The book gestures at weighty ideas—identity, power, sacrifice—but never digs into them. Every time it sets up a moral dilemma or a philosophical question, it either dodges it with a convenient plot twist or explains it away in a paragraph. I kept waiting for the narrative to slow down and wrestle with its own implications, but it just barrels forward on plot mechanics. The conflict feels manufactured; the stakes are high in theory but hollow in practice because we never truly understand why anyone believes what they do.

I’ve read other works by this author, and they handled nuance much better. This one reads like a rushed first draft that needed another round of revision to deepen the characters and the world. It’s not a terrible read—the prose is competent and the pacing keeps you turning pages—but I finished it feeling unsatisfied, as if I’d eaten a meal with no flavor. If you’re looking for something thought-provoking or emotionally resonant, look elsewhere. This is a shallow pool dressed up to look like an ocean.

Written 40 years ago, in a story with no non-Whites, it was still acceptable to talk about racial/tribal community as a natural and healthy thing. However, the true testament to this pencil is not in its grip or its eraser, but it’s durability. This pencil and I survived high school together. I changed more than this pencil did. It encountered more drops, people, missed Hail Mary passes, and physics exams that any other writing utensil I have ever owned. It was stolen and returned more times than I could count—lost and then found even more than that. I’m convinced that this pencil has the life span of a styrofoam cup in a landfill. Buy this pencil, because you’re buying more than a pencil here: you’re buying something that you could quite possible carry through an entire era of your life. And maybe one day, you will look down at that Graph Gear 1000 and reminisce on all the memories you made holding that pencil.

title: It can't 'bump' automatically when the water is boiled, ...
text:
I bought this kettle hoping for the convenience of an automatic shut-off when the water reaches a boil. Unfortunately, it does not bump or click off on its own as advertised. You have to stand by and watch it, or set a separate timer, which kind of defeats the purpose. The heating element works fine, and the stainless steel body looks nice on the counter, but the lack of an auto-off feature is a real letdown, especially since the product description implied it would.

On the plus side, the handle stays cool, the spout pours without dripping, and the capacity is generous for making tea or coffee for the family. It heats water reasonably quickly, though not as fast as some higher-end models I have used. The lid fits snugly, and the finish seems durable so far after a few weeks of daily use.

My main frustration is the manual monitoring required. If you get distracted, the water can keep boiling, wasting energy and creating excess steam that fogs up the kitchen. For a product in this price range, I expected better automation. It is not a terrible kettle, but it does not deliver on the promise of a bump or automatic switch-off. I would rate it three stars because it works as a basic kettle, but I would not recommend it if you want true hands-off operation. For the same money, there are better options with reliable auto-shutoff features.

title: Great Book!
text:
I picked up "Great Book!" based on the title alone — yes, I was that curious. And honestly, for the most part, it lives up to its name. The writing style is engaging and conversational, which made it easy to get through in just a few sittings. The author covers some fascinating ideas, blending personal anecdotes with solid research in a way that never feels dry. I found myself highlighting several passages and even dog-earing a few pages to revisit later.

What keeps it from a full five stars for me is the pacing in the middle section. Around chapters four through six, the narrative loses a bit of steam. The concepts start to feel repetitive, and I wished the author had either tightened that part or introduced a fresh angle sooner. It picks back up nicely in the final chapters, but that middle lull took some effort to push through.

Also, a minor but noticeable issue: the paperback edition I received had a few smudged print lines in one chapter. Nothing unreadable, but slightly disappointing for a new book.

Overall, "Great Book!" is a solid, thought-provoking read that I’d recommend to anyone interested in the subject. Just be prepared for a brief slowdown before the strong finish. Worth the money, but not quite a flawless gem.

With her ususal excellent style and story telling skills, Ruth Rendell introduces us to a petty criminal and the effect he has on several of his victoms--lonely, vulnerable women. Because of that, Rendell's novels carry some form of social significance that take them beyond the mystery level. And as usual, this book is a page turner.
However, in this particular novel, she has too many characters and, respectively, too many social issues/implications going on that do not always come together as planned. We have a gay MP that is relevied when he is forced to come out (social responsibiltry vs. personal freedom), his wife who is not necessarily a bad mother to her kids, but still really dumb (feminist ideas vs. traditional upbringing dilemmas); a couple with opposite eating disorders that somehow get cured abd their relationship with their friend who unvoluntarily implcates them in a crime (friednship and betrayal); and all of the above are not related too much to the mystery. title: Very happy to finally lay hands on one it is now ...
text:
Very happy to finally lay hands on one it is now sitting in my game room next to my other favorites. I have been watching this item come back in and out of stock for months, and every time I hesitated, it vanished before I could check out. When I saw the restock notification this time, I jumped on it immediately, and I am so glad I did.

I am writing this review after three full plays with a group of four adults, plus one solo run to learn the rules. The components are absolutely gorgeous – the card stock is thick with a linen finish that feels premium, the tokens are chunky, and the artwork on everything is vibrant without being overly busy. The rulebook is clearly laid out, which is a huge relief because I have had to teach many complicated games that required constant rule lookups. This one took about ten minutes to explain, and by the second round everyone was strategizing on their own.

What really sets this game apart is the balance between luck and planning. You can have a perfect strategy, but a few unlucky draws can push you to adapt on the fly, which keeps every session fresh. The replay value seems immense. There are multiple character abilities, variable setup options, and a scoring system that rewards different play styles – aggressive builders, cautious explorers, and even sneaky traders all have viable paths to victory. My last game came down to a single point, and the table erupted into friendly arguments about who should have blocked whom. That is the mark of a great game.

The only minor criticism I have is that the box insert could be a little more efficient; the plastic trays leave some pieces loose if you store it vertically. But that is a small nitpick for such a well-crafted product. For anyone on the fence, do not wait. This one sells out fast for a reason, and I can already tell it will be hitting our table regularly for years to come. If you love medium-weight strategy games with a bit of social interaction, this is a must-buy. Five stars without hesitation.
