title: Fits my Mosin Nagant 91/30
text:
I bought this specifically for my Mosin Nagant 91/30, and I have to say, it fits like a glove. I’ve been through a few different accessories for this old warhorse, and nothing has been this precise right out of the box. The machining is clean, and it doesn’t wobble or shift even after a full day at the range. Installation took me about fifteen minutes with basic tools, and I didn’t have to file or shim anything. The finish matches the rifle’s aesthetic without looking out too modern, which I appreciate since I try to keep my Mosin looking period-correct-ish.

I’ve put about a hundred rounds through it since mounting, and it holds zero perfectly. Recoil on a 91/30 is no joke, but this thing stays put. The locking mechanism is solid, and I don’t worry about it loosening up mid-session. I’ve used it with both surplus light ball and modern soft point hunting loads, and performance is consistent.

The only minor thing is that it adds a bit of weight, but that’s expected with anything steel. For the price, the quality is impressive. If you’ve been fighting with cheap alternatives or jury-rigged setups, just get this. It saves time, frustration, and ammo. I’m honestly surprised more Mosin owners aren’t talking about this. It turns a rough-and-tumble surplus rifle into a genuinely accurate shooter.5-yard capable shooter. Highly recommend for anyone who wants to upgrade their Mosin without compromising reliability or authenticity. Five stars, no question.

title: Limited, superficial, and incomplete (for those who know0
text:
For those who don't know the depth and breadth of Qigong as field of endeavor (not a singular art) with very diverse practices, this is a taste-tester's manual on the topic concerning one of the oldest Qigong systems on record. The problem is ...

(1) it only covers two of the five animals from the ancient sage physician Hua Tou. Which means one's practice is incomplete and out of balance for this particular system.

(2) that no modern scholars are truly certain of how these exercises were conducted, since we have only the sage physician's written descriptions (and not extensive ones) mixed with some cave drawings, and

(3) there are better works that attempt to address not only their own speculations on how these exercises were conducted but also attempt to support such with scholarship and reasoning, drawing on comparative arts inside and outside of the Qigong field, and stepping well beyond mere two sentence sketchy definitions of romanized Chinese terms... as is the case in this book.

If you would like a simple and short manual with direct instructions for soft exercises that might not do enough for you, then maybe this is for you. Or if you're another new ager looking for your next step on a path likely leading nowhere, then this is for you. If you want to explore the range of speculations on this ancient Qigong system, then you might also consider buying it... but only after you've acquired other more comprehensive works on the topic.

title: Something of a Find
text:
I'm very happy with this cart, and two reasons stand out: its sturdiness and its size.

It's a very clever design, and the parts are of high quality. The result is a rigid structure that's perfect for applications like mine: support for a wide-carriage "pro" printer that can be placed on the top shelf without the somewhat massive printhead action causing side-to-side sway.

The size is a difficult one to find elsewhere. In my case I needed to replace a cheap TV cart made of low-density fiberboard and formica. I was using it to support not only the aforementoned wide printer on top but also a laser printer and scanner on the lower shelf. Any replacement would have to be almost the same size because of my office setup. I was ready to give up -- most shelving/carts like these are dimensioned in multiples of 12 inches -- but then I found this guy (the 16x28). Perfect! A little taller than the crumbling TV cart, but that's OK. I gained a third shelf for supplies that previously lived on the carpet under the cart.

One problem (for me): Carts like these have no sides onto which you can stick things -- in my case USB hubs. The solution was fairly simple: pegboard material cut to size, held in place with toggle bolts (with shortened screws).

One caution: unlike wood shelf units, which typically have uniform shelf width front to back, carts like these have tubing at the four corners that you might need to take into account. If your printer, for example, is a tight fit on one of the lower shelves, it might fit fine and work fine but not allow you to pull out the paper supply drawer if you can't skooch it over. The inner post-clearing distances for the shelves in this case is about 25.5 inches (left-to-right as pictured) and about 13.5 inches (front-to-back as pictured).

Regarding ease of assembly... Yes, the instructions are terse, but it's not rocket science. If you have a third-grader in the house, you should be fine.

All in all, a very satisfactory purchase and a good value.

title: Good noise suppression and durability for a fantastic price
text:
I bought these after looking through various first- and third-party solutions for low-noise Mavic Pro props. I'm using them on an original Mavic Pro (not a Platinum) and I absolutely love them for 3 reasons:

1, they make a big difference in terms of the Mavic's sound output. I haven't done formal tests with a decibel meter, but it's obvious that the flights are significantly quieter with these props both indoors and out. I now tend to have some trouble hearing my Mavic once it's up to about 150-200ft even when directly overhead (though obviously quick altitude changes or movements change that). It's made it much less obtrusive than the original props. I haven't tried other brands and therefore can't compare to other manufacturers' low-noise props, but you'll definitely notice a big improvement over the stock blades.

2, their durability seems just as good as the original props'. I read several reviews of other low-noise props that complained that the gold tips were made of a softer, more easily deformed plastic. That isn't the case with these, as it's the same material along the entire length. That may make a slight difference when it comes to aerodynamics, but it means I don't have to worry about them when folding up the props (by the way, they fold up just fine despite their slightly larger size, as long as you're a little careful when unfolding the back legs and don't get the pairs intertwined). The paint scuffs relatively easily, but that's it. I've replaced one set after stupidly crashing into some scrubby branches, but even then there were only a few minor nicks and gouges that I probably could have gotten away still flying with, but at this price it's stupid not to just get another set.

3, obviously the price is amazing. These are half the price of all other manufacturers' props that I could find, and at $8 for a complete set it's really hard to argue with when you get such significant noise reduction. I can't imagine going back to anything else. I'd buy 2 sets just to have some spares.

A good portion of the story deals with the fallout that is created in the remaining family members when a child goes missing. The part that is similar to other works of fiction deals with how the family copes, when the hoped for miracle happens: the child returns to the family many years later, eliciting both joy and suspicion. The suspicion is driven by thoughts that the returning child (unrecognizable, after so many years) may, in fact, be an imposter.

The author has curated a list of words--four for each letter of the alphabet--and explains how it is used and how it came to be used. As the author notes in the introduction, words have personalities, and this book explores them. Did you ever wonder why a British policeman is called a Bobby? Why the yellow weeds we see everywhere are called dandelions? Why long races are called marathons or why it's called a quarantine when people are kept separate from others? This book explains all these words and many more, including some that are definitely not in the average grade school vocabulary. Although the book is published in the United States, there are many words used more commonly in Great Britain and a fair amount that may seem a bit archaic, but readers still learn about everyday words like pajamas and shampoo. It's a great choice for encouraging creativity, enlarging and enriching a child's vocabulary, and for that kiddo that just loves knowing all sorts of off-beat and fascinating facts. Grownups reading along with them should be prepared to be surprised and educated, too.

I read the reviews before I bought these. I honestly was not sure whether I'd be making a good purchase or not.

The price was right, and my VBS budget was rapidly shrinking- in fact, I decided to buy them out of pocket, because I thought it would be helpful.
Well, after 5 days of exploring, tumbling, game-playing, etc with kids ages 5-11, I'd say this was excellent value for my money. I only used the included cards for certain ones, since we color-coded the name tags for identifiability, but the card stock which is included, is of a really good quality. I have passed them on to our missions team, and they will use them!

Did they all make it thorough the 5 days? No. About 5 of the lanyards broke, but we just knot-tied them, and they were good to go. The rest made it through.

So if you are looking for an inexpensive option, that can withstand some rough and tumble, this is for you.

Edit: After I wrote this review, I spent an office day going through all my VBS supplies, and feel that I need to amend my review to reflect the following.
I had gone through the badges before, and they appeared to be in good shape. On closer examination, I found that almost all of them had been tied with a knot. So I guess that although as a whole, they lasted for the five days, and withstood, as I said, a LOT of rough and tumble, I have very few that I will in good conscience use next year. I will reuse some, but only as backups.

So, If you're not using them for children, and don't particularly care if you get to reuse them, it's still value for money.

I still feel that the value may have been lost to me, due to the fact that I will definitely have to buy more next year, I did save a significant amount during THIS budget period.

title: It's not about food
text:
Differently from the movie, this is not a tale about sophisticated food. It deals with the severe restrictions that puritanism imposes on pleasure - and how a tastefull dinner, with the help of some good wines, helps this fundamentalist lutheran aging community to retrieve joy and forgiveness.

In the movie, although the puritan restrictions are present, stress is on the food - the ingredients, the way it is being prepared, the discovery of it by the coachman and Bebette's assitant, and principally the precise description by the general. The transformation of the puritans, from mere tolerance of an extravagance to real appreciation and joy only underines the quality of what is being served.

In the novel, food plays a secondary role, contrasting with the grey sad environment and the equally gray and sad inhabitants of a norwegian community lost in the high north, squeezed between the mountains and an unfriendly see. Stress is on the way a severe pastor has molded the spirit of his daughters and of his few followers, banning all earthly pleasures.

I've decided to read the novel after having a dinner that reproduced the menu of Babette's feast, preceded by the film and a technical explanation by the danish chef. Dinner was excelent and our community did not resemble at all to the inhabitants of the small village - which in the film was moved from Norway to Denmark. I was first surprised by the differences in approach but then I realized that this short novel gives you food for thoughts. While the movie is pure pleasure, the novel is profound.

I recommend it and, if I may suggest, have it complete: the movie, the dinner and the short novel.

title: Original fantasy with strong world building and characters
text:
Full disclosure: I won this in a Goodreads giveaway.

It's very, very rare to come across a truly original entry in the epic fantasy world, these days. Though in some ways I'm not even sure fantasy describes this book. Yes, it's obviously fantasy with magic and different races and such things, but at the same time it doesn't seem to focus on those things. It doesn't have the 'feel' of a typical fantasy book, and to me that's a good thing. Perhaps because it lacks some of the heaviness that many serious fantasy novels have. I did find that to be a good thing, though. It let the story move fairly quickly without getting bogged down on small details.

The world itself is very well laid out, especially because the reader is discovering it as the main character does. Rather clever of the author, there. Didn't even occur to me as I was reading, but in retrospect it worked and was very entertaining.

Characters...complex, interesting, well-rounded. I could go on, but you get the idea. At no point did I get the feeling I was dealing with cut outs or your typical fantasy cliches. Though I'll admit I'm a sucker for an anti-hero, which the main character definitely is. The relationships throughout the story are just as interesting, and nothing is ever quite as it seems.

I found the story itself to be very compelling and very original. It was one of those books that I couldn't wait to pick up when I had to set it down to go do something else. Halfway through I found myself lamenting the fact that there aren't any other books in the series written yet. I'm not going to talk much about it because there really is a lot to give away. I, for one, did not see the twists coming.

I really look forward to the next book in the series and finding out more about these characters, as well as the world they live in. Unlike so many books, these days, there's a very satisfying ending to this tale. Yes, it's apparently part of a larger story arc, but the author has not neglected the necessary resolution in each smaller part.

title: Not Recommended for Screenwriters
text:
I wouldn't recommend this resource for aspiring screenwriters. I had hoped that this book might offer some off-beat advice, but instead it quoted Goldman's classic Adventures in the Screen Trade and made endless references to film examples without much explanation.

In order to get much out of it, I think you have to be extremely well-versed in the films they are referencing, some of which are rightfully obscure (given the aim of the book), some of which are not great examples, and many of which are dated (many come from the 90s, presumably leftover from the original edition). While the authors attempt efforts to add some updates and expand their analysis to television, digital media, foreign, and independent films, I did not find their words particularly useful. Deep into the book, there is also some very basic screenwriting advice (formatting, etc.), which seems out of place.

I'm always hesitant to take screenwriting advice from non-professional screenwriters, as these authors are. Even from a film analysis perspective, I was not impressed with their insight here. Although the pursuit of non-traditional scriptwriting is admirable, I would look elsewhere.

title: If I Stay
text:
In If I Stay, we meet Mia, a very talented cellist, who is in love with a boy who wants to be a rock star. They find their lives being pulled in two different directions. Mia hopes to go to Juilliard and Adam, her boyfriend, hopes to take his band to the highest points in the industry. Until everything changes for both of them. Mia's family is in a car accident and then she is left in a coma. While her body lies limp in a hospital bed, she finds herself taking a journey to figure out if she should leave everything on earth behind to be with her family, who are already gone, or stay and be with those who are there praying and hoping she will return. This story isn't just about love and loss, its about impossible choices and heartbreak. No matter what Mia's choice, she feels that she loses a piece of herself.

We follow Mia througout the book on a journey through her memories, making you better understand how badly she will break if she wakes up and has lost her family. We also see her relationship with Adam and how much they truly care about each other and how their lives are clearly drifting in different directions.This story is painful just to read but beautifully written and really hits its mark in making you sit at the edge of your seat to see which avenue she will choose.

title: Didn’t Hold Up As Promised
text:
I really wanted to like this product, especially given the positive reviews and the promise of durability. For the first week or so, it seemed fine. My dog is a medium-sized chewer, nothing too aggressive, just a normal chewer who likes to gnaw on things. The material felt sturdy out of the box and I was optimistic.

But after about two weeks, the seams started pulling apart. I followed the care instructions exactly, didn't leave it out in the rain, and only used it indoors only. By the third week, there was a noticeable tear along split where the stitching came undone. For the price I paid, I expected at least a few months of regular season's use. It simply didn't hold up as advertised.

The worst part is that my dog didn't even go after it that hard. It's not like she was shredding it daily. Just normal use and it fell apart. The manufacturer claims heavy-duty construction, but that's not what I experienced. The padding inside also flattened out of the box was comfortable, but quickly flattened out too. I have had cheaper items from other brands last twice as long.

Overall, a letdown. If your pet is extremely gentle and barely touches their things, maybe this works. But if you have an average, playful dog, look elsewhere. It looks great in the photos, but real-world use is disappointing. I can't recommend spending your money on this.

title: Not exactly comfortable for the dog.
text:
I bought this bed hoping my golden retriever would finally have a cozy spot to rest after long walks. The photos online looked plush and inviting, but the reality is very different. The filling is thin and uneven, and after just a week, it had already flattened in the middle. My dog, who’s about 55 pounds, circles it endlessly trying to find a comfortable position, and often ends up lying on the floor instead. The memory foam claim feels like a joke—there’s virtually no support. I can feel the hard floor through the pad when I press down.

The material itself isn’t great either. It’s that stiff, crinkly polyester that makes noise every time the dog shifts. He seems a bit anxious on it, probably because it sounds like a rustling bag under him. The non-slip bottom doesn’t work on my hardwood floors; the whole thing slides around if he jumps on or off. Washing is a hassle—the cover zipper broke on the second wash, and now it’s impossible to remove without tearing.

I wanted to love this, and my dog deserves a nice bed, but this just isn’t it. He’s back to using an old blanket on the couch. For the price, I expected at least basic comfort, not something that looks good in pictures but performs poorly. I’ll be returning it and trying a different brand. Hopefully others have better luck, but for us, it’s a miss.

Production--the use of reason to create material values--is the central activity that makes our lives possible. To condemn profit is to condemn production, and to condemn production is to condemn human life. But many do condemn profit.

The key issue is that profits earned through voluntary trade, no matter how large, require no special justification. They are good because they make the producer who earns them better off. To quote political philosopher Isabel Paterson: "If profit is denounced, it must be assumed that running at a loss is admirable."

Most of the ideas in this book are the direct opposite of the Marxist or socialist maxims being promoted by the Obama administration. If Obama's ideas scare you I think you'll enjoy the book.

I’ve been looking for a piece that would tie together the empty wall above my console table without being too fussy or trendy, and this “Great decoration” was exactly what I needed. The moment I unboxed it, I was impressed by the quality was evident. The materials feel substantial—not flimsy or plasticky like some items in this price range. The finish is smooth and consistent, with no rough edges or uneven paint. It arrived well-packaged, so there was no damage during shipping, which is always a relief.

I hung it in my living room, and it immediately became the focal point of the space. The design is balanced enough to complement both my modern furniture and the warmer, textured accents I have. It doesn’t scream for attention, but it definitely draws the eye in a pleasant way. I’ve received several compliments from guests who asked where I found it. One friend thought it was a custom piece. That says a lot.

Installation was straightforward. The back has a simple yet secure hanging system—no need to hunt for extra hardware. It sat level right out of the box. I appreciate that the dimensions are generous without being overwhelming. It fills up the wall without overwhelming it. I was a little worried it might look too small based on the product photos, but the size is perfect for a standard wall section. It also works well above a side table and also a larger than a mirror or a set of frames.

Color-wise, the tones are slightly more muted than I expected from the listing images, but in a good way. They blend seamlessly with the room rather than clashing. It works well with both warm and cool lighting. Under my dimmable overhead, it looks elegant; during the day with natural light, it feels airy and fresh.

For the price, I honestly expected something nice but not this nice. It feels like a premium piece that I would have spent twice as much on at a boutique store. If you’re on the fence, just go for it. It’s one of those rare home decor buys that exceeds your expectations and makes you smile every time you walk past. I’m already thinking about buying another for my bedroom. Highly recommend for anyone wanting to add a subtle, stylish statement without the hassle.

title: Opened my EYES!
text:
I have to admit, I picked up this book with a fair amount of skepticism. The title "Opened my EYES!" felt a bit dramatic, and I wasn't sure what to expect. But after reading it, I can honestly say it's the most accurate description possible. This book genuinely shifted the way I see things. It's not often that a single volume can change your entire perspective on something you thought you understood, but that's exactly what happened here.

The author presents complex ideas in a way that feels accessible and deeply personal. I found myself nodding along, then stopping to reread passages because they hit so close to home. What I appreciated most is that it doesn't just point out problems it offers practical ways to see them differently. The chapters are well-structured, each building on each other without becoming repetitive. There were moments when I actually felt a sense of relief realizing that the patterns I had been stuck in for years were not unique to me.

If you are someone who feels like you've been going through life on autopilot, or if you've ever wondered why certain situations keep repeating, this book is for you. It's not a quick fix, but it's a powerful starting point. I've already recommended it to three friends and plan to read it again to absorb the parts I might have missed. For anyone on the fence, just get it. It lives up to its title in the most honest way possible.

title: How a "LUNATEC" made me break up with my former flame, Scrub Daddy.
text: We have a large-breed dog (Akita) Rescue and wash lots of dog bowls. We first fell in love with Scrub Daddy because you can use it over and over again with no mildew smell. At first, we were willing to forgive the high price for the little happy face on "daddy" but rather quickly, too quickly, in fact, his face went from happy to sad. In fact, he was downright distraught while sitting on the counter and he flopped around in our hand making it difficult to use. We then stumbled on the Lunatec. Yes, it's a little different. Like a dish cloth but ...more...nylon-netty and flimsy. But that's what makes it perfect! The Luncatec can lay across a finger tip and wipe inside a water bottle or other small area, lay flat and wash out a large water trough or bowl, or, fold it in half or quarters for a scrub-pad effect. A Scrub Buddy, with average use (used twice a day on 6 bowls) lasted about 2 weeks. So far, the Lunatec has been here and after nearly 3 weeks, shows ZERO signs of wear. No smell, no scudge, no bacteria. Just clean, clean, scrubbing and clean clean bowls. Oh, we noted another reviewer was unhappy with the Lunatec because he said he washed out a bowl with bread dough and it clogged the Lunatec. Well, duh, or, should we say "Doh!" You should expect that result with ANY type of sponge or cloth and a gooey/gummy dough. When we make bread or macaroni and cheese and have gooey bowls, we use plastic pan scrapers or a hard sink brush to knock off all the gooey/gummy stuff first and then use a sponge or cloth to do the washing/sanitizing. One Scrub Daddy for $8.50 or FOUR (4) Lunatec's for $7.50. The choice is simple, we think. This product stands up, does MORE than it should, and for that, we love you, you Lunatec!

title: A Pop Up Book to Explore with Several Senses
text:
In our family, we have loved pop-up books for several generations, including examples from more than a century ago that are beloved volumes on our bookshelf to this day. While this third book has zero holiday content, we immediately recognized ABC Pop-Up as a marvelous choice for holiday gift-giving.

This pop-up book brilliantly invites adults and children to explore several senses: sound, vision and even tactile experiences of exploring the pop up shapes!

My favorite sequence is a pop-up bed that stands up in front of us, as we read the book, without any immediate clue as to the letters involved. Then, if we closely examine the bed, we discover the pillow has an embossed P in one corner and the quilt has an embossed Q. Little fingers can touch the letters and actually feel the raised shapes.

Then, the sequence continues with a stately tree that leaps up with an attached tire swing and, as we look over the entire page, we discover that we can glimpse the tree’s gnarled roots at the bottom of the page. What letters are we discovering? The tire swing actually dangles from a string and, if our eyes are quick, we can see the S for swing. But what about R? Little fingers can detect an embossed R in the tree’s roots. And then what’s the T? Well, you can guess.

In our family collection, we now own more than 100 pop up books and, while this book is, indeed, little in its physical scale, it is truly a work of genius!

title: Modern pulp SciFi, with a lot of fun
text: This book is a throwback to the good old days of scifi, with lots of weird aliens, some (fairly) heroic protagonists and a (sort of) quest. The characters are well-drawn, and individual, but they are archetypal, the quest is rather mundane but needed, and the world building is relatively believable. The biggest difference from the earlier pulp fiction is that humans are the least and most recent of the members of the governing Galactic Commons (the GC) with other aliens having much better technology, more advanced civilizations, and a bigger impact on the universe. Humans are acceptable, but it is obvious we are often just tolerated in this world. It is a different take, and an interesting one. I liked the people, I enjoyed the story, and the exciting bits were fine. There is not a lot of back story on how humans became a part of the GC, or what happened to Earth and why humans came to be wandering around seeking a new home, or how they were discovered by the aliens; it is a given from the start. The nine member crew of the Wayfarer contains 5 humans, the owner, two techs (one mechanical, one comp), a clerk, and a fuel specialist (algae is used, and it requires a full-time person to monitor the vats to keep it going); three alien members, a reptile pilot, a bug-like medic/chef, and a fur-covered navigator; and a sapient AI that basically runs the ship. The interactions of the crew and their friends make up much of the book, with some of their backgrounds giving more history. It is a fun read, and I enjoyed it, I was also pleased that there were going to be other books in the series. If you enjoyed the good old days, read this book.

title: Eh, its ok
text: This is kinda a weird item.  Neat idea, but weird.  I have extended magazines that came with my Sig pistol and they fit okay.  The problem with extended mags is they don't fit in most mag holders because they are overly tall and the flap doesn't velcro shut like it should.  The flaps on this pouch grab the velcro with my mags inside, but just barely.  You can fold the flaps back entirely and use the "griptite" feature to hold the magazines.  I keep going back and forth on whether I like the "griptite" design.  It consists of plastic clips that grab the magazines, which fold into the cordura material in a pocket.  Hard to explain, but when you put your mag in the plastic acts as a spring and squeezes your magazine.  The mag slides out with a mild tug.  They make the overall pouch much thicker, probably twice as thick as the magazine would be otherwise.  I think I would prefer a simple pouch over a gee-whiz clippy thing.  I suspect these would be great if you knew you would be standing up while using them (such as on the range or at a match).  If you were crawling around in the dirt with these they still might fall out (even with the "griptite" feature) and your magazines would certainly get dirty.  These are not great for keeping your mags out of the elements.  But i suppose it's a trade off.  They are quite speedy to get out and would make for quick mag changes.  They're cheap enough- try them out for yourself!

I bought the Lois Good on the Counter hoping it would help me organize my small kitchen, and overall it does the job. The design-wise, but there are a few things to note. title: Good to have on hand for emergencies
text:
I bought this a few months ago after a close call during a solo hike. I wasp on a remote trail. I wanted something compact that I could toss in my daypack and forget about until I really needed it. This fits that bill perfectly. The kit is not bulky at all it easily slides into the side pocket of my backpack or even my glove compartment without taking up much space.

The first thing I checked was the quality of the included tools. The knife is surprisingly sharp out of the box, the whistle is loud enough to hear from a good distance, and the fire starter works as intended. I tested the emergency blanket on a chilly evening just to see how much heat it reflects. It actually works. The compass is simple but functional for basic orientation. The little paracord is also came in handy for tying down a tarp when a sudden squall hit.

What I appreciate most is that nothing feels cheap or flimsy. For the components are well-made and packed securely. I have no doubt that if I were stuck out overnight this would keep me safe and comfortable until rescue. It gives peace of mind knowing I have a small but capable survival tool that does not require me to carry a heavy load.

I would recommend this to anyone who hikes, campers, or anyone who spends time outdoors. It also makes a thoughtful gift for friends just starting to explore backcountry. The price is more than fair for the quality. For the cost of a couple of fancy coffee drinks you are really getting a reliable backup plan in a tiny package. I have already bought a feeling I will never actually need to use it in a dire situation, but it is comforting to know it is there if I do. Five stars without hesitation.

It’s not a pattern book, though it does have dozens already. Instead, it’s a deep, thoughtful exploration of the history, culture, and craft of yarn itself. The author has a gift for storytelling, which is fitting since “yarn” literally means a good tale. Each chapter weaves together the origins of different fibers from sheep farming in the Shetlands to small-batch indigo dyeing in Japan along with profiles of spinners, dyers, and designers I’d never heard of. I learned why some wool feels scratchy and others drape like silk, how yarn thickness is measured internationally, and even the surprising role of yarn-related superstitions from various traditions.

The writing is warm and personal, not dry or academic. It felt like sitting with a knowledgeable friend who just happens to be obsessed with fiber science. The photos are gorgeous, but not just pretty pictures they actually illustrate the text. I’ve already tried two new spinning techniques and a dye method using onion skins after reading about it here. My knitting group passed this around, and everyone came away with something different: one friend started researching local fleece suppliers; another finally understood why her merino pills.

If you love yarn, or if you love great writing about making things, this book belongs on your shelf. It made me appreciate every skein I own just a little more.

title: more lets sticker and paste
text:
I bought this for my three-year-old, who is obsessed with stickers but tends to lose focus with more complicated craft kits. "More Lets Sticker and Paste" has been a fantastic addition to our quiet-time rotation. The book arrived in great condition, with sturdy pages that can withstand a bit of enthusiastic peeling and repositioning. What I appreciate most ishike most is the balance between open-ended creativity and gentle guidance. Each spread presents a simple scene—a garden, a kitchen, a fish tank—and provides a set of stickers and cutout shapes that your child can place however they like, but with enough structure that they don't get overwhelmed.

My son spent a solid thirty minutes on the first page alone, meticulously moving a frog from a lily pad to a flower, then back again. The paste portion is equally engaging. The book includes perforated paper pieces that you can tear out, and we used a basic glue stick to attach them. It is messier than stickers, but the activity encourages fine motor skills and planning: where does the apple go on the tree? Should the bird be in the sky or on the ground? The instructions are minimal, which I appreciate because it lets my child lead.

One thing that surprised me is how much we talk during these activities. He narrates what he is doing, and I ask questions about his choices. It feels less like a workbook and more like a shared experience. The book is also thick enough to last through many sessions. We have used about half the pages in two weeks, and the remaining ones are still crisp. I have already ordered another for a friend's birthday. If you have a toddler or preschooler who loves hands-on play, this is a no-brainer. It is screen-free, low-prep, and genuinely fun for both of us. Highly recommend.

title: Twisty Rods for Beachy Waves or Coily Curls
text:
My hair has lots of different kinds of curls in it, from tight coils near the nape of my neck, to spirals, all the way to slightly wavy hair at the crown of my head. I get a more consistent curl when I use curlers! I've been using large foam curlers for a while to get large, uniform waves that straighten out over a few days, but I wanted to try a curler that would give me tighter curls.

The Ohuhu Twist Flex Rods come with 7 different curl sizes, and each size has 6 rollers. The rollers are color-coded by size, so you think I'd be able to find all 7 curlers, but apparently I thought there were only 6 when I took the picture. I'd never used these kinds of curlers before, but they were simple to use. I used the two largest sizes, and took a small section of hair and put the end of it in the middle of a roller. Then, I rolled the hair up into the roller, making sure to keep the hair in the center of the rod. Twisting the ends together keeps the curler in place.

I tried to let my hair air-dry with the curlers in, but I have a LOT of hair, and knew that could take days, so after a few hours, I put on my bonnet dryer and finished the job. I was pretty happy with my ringlets! I did muss them up for a nice, beachy curly-wave, too. I really liked getting the curl all the way to my crown, and how much lift it gave the top of my 'do. And, the curls weren't tangly like my hair can get if I let it completely air dry. I could run my fingers through them and get a messy, beachy wave - and still no frizz or tangles.

(I received this product for review purposes. My opinions are my own. For more information and pictures, please see my blog, Lit From Within.)

text:
Katelin has found some peace and finds she looks forward to returning and spending the summer with her grandmother. Alone, without Simon, Katelin not only finds her own adventure but encounters a young man who sends flutters through her stomach. Through the journey, Katelin and her elfin friends discover how deeply her loyalty, fearlessness and determination runs. Together they must overcome the tyrant of the Elfin world and keep the Orb out of his grasp. The only question is, is Katelin strong enough or will she bite off more than she can handle?

What a fantastic fantasy! I enjoyed the first book but was blown away by the second. Sharon Dwyer set the "worlds" up very well, the characters were very well developed; Katelin was perfect! Dwyer captured Katelin’s "attitude" and emotional well-being accurately. Dwyer skillfully wrote the stories so that her readers do/will connect with Katelin in one way or another. The connection between the worlds was realistically done - meaning the characters had believable crossover and purpose. The first book was excellent!

The second book, I LOVED! I enjoy reading books where the female character is strong without knowing it. Piney, while not a cute character in real life, became adorable and perfect for Katelin. Dwyer expertly built up the suspense between the two books and the characters. I am intrigued on how Nana and the other worlds play out in Katelin's birthright ... I suspect a twist somewhere!

Dwyer’s The Fastasmagorical Forest series is exciting, inviting and mesmerizing. Once you get into the books, there is no stepping away. Lots of fun, plot twists, and adventure.

Very well done! While a book for young adults, those of us who enjoy fantasy, magic and adventure will love this book as well! I cannot wait for the series to continue!!!

title: Sparks creativity, once you get past install problems
text:
The Digital Arts & Craft Studio from Fisher-Price is fun for the whole family (I think I used it more the first night than my 3 year old!), but you may be driven crazy by problems with the install process. Buyer beware if you are not willing to troubleshoot potential problems with buggy software.

In my case, I received the "Common Language Runtime Debugging error." If you do too, and your system meets the minimum requirements (and the firmware test, which comes with the software, works) then the problem is most likely your Microsoft .NET Framework installation.

I had 1.1 installed and it appears the program installs both a hotfix and .NET 2.0. To fix: uninstall everything (add/Remove programs). First, the Studio software, then NET 2.0, then the hotfix, and finally NET 1.1. Reboot, and reinstall from the CD. Everything should now work.

Took about an hour, but then we were up and running. Is it worth the money? My toddler is fascinated by the computer, and loves to draw, making this toy the perfect combination to keep her occupied (at least for a little while).

title: Pet Favorite
text:
I’ve gone through three different beds for my golden retriever, Milo, and none of them lasted more than a few months. He’s a chewer and a digger, so I was skeptical when I ordered the Pet Favorite. But after six weeks of daily use, I’m genuinely impressed. The cover is a thick, rip-stop fabric that has held up against his determined scratching and the occasional excited zoomie session. No tears, no loose threads. The inner cushion is plush enough for him to sink into but firm enough to provide proper support—he’s a senior dog with mild hip stiffness, and I’ve noticed he gets up much more easily in the mornings since we switched.

What really sold me is the washability. The first time he had an accident. I unzipped the cover, tossed it in the wash on cold, and it came out looking like new. No shrinking, no pilling, or fading. The waterproof inner liner did its job perfectly the mattress pad underneath stayed completely dry. That alone makes it worth the price.

The size is generous too. Milo is about 75 pounds and he has plenty of room to sprawl out or curl into a tight ball. The raised edges are high enough to rest his head on, which he loves. No funky chemical smell out of the box either just a faint fabric scent that disappeared after a day.

I honestly wasn’t expecting to love this bed as much as my dog does. He spends hours on it every day, and even our cat has claimed a corner. If you’re tired replacing pet beds every season, give this one a shot. It’s sturdy, comfortable, and easy to clean exactly what we needed.

title: Fail
text:
I bought the "Fail" pet bed thinking the name was just a quirky marketing gimmick. Unfortunately, it turned out to be a pretty accurate description. The bed looked great in the photos, but in reality the foam padding is far thinner than advertised. My 25-pound terrier sinks right through to the floor within minutes. I followed the care instructions exactly, but after two machine washes the outer cover started pilling and the zipper broke. For a product marketed as a premium pet supply, the build quality is disappointing.

On the positive side, the fabric is soft and my dog does seem to enjoy curling up on it when I fluff the filling back into shape. The non-skid bottom works reasonably well on hardwood floors. However, the bed does not hold its form; it looks lumpy and sad after a week of use. At this price point, I expected something that would last longer. I've had cheaper beds from other brands that held up for years.

Maybe this would work for a very small, lightweight cat or a toy breed that doesn't move around much. For any dog that actually sleeps hard, it's not worth the money. I'll be replacing it within a few months. The name "Fail" is unfortunately fitting.

title: Ok product
text:
I picked this up a few weeks ago when my old desk organizer finally gave out. The price was reasonable, so I figured I'd give it a shot. Overall, it's not a bad product by for anything too complex, but for basic day-to-day office supplies, it gets the job done. Assembly was fairly straightforward, though the instructions could be clearer. It took me about fifteen minutes to put together, which is fine, but I did notice a few of the screw holes didn't line up perfectly. These quite line up perfectly on the first try. Not a deal breaker, but something to note.

The build quality is what I'd call "OK" in the title. It's sturdy enough to hold pens, paperclips, sticky notes, and a small notepad without flexing too much. The material feels like it will hold up for daily use, but I wouldn't trust it with anything heavy like a stapler or a large binder clip. The finish is matte and does a decent job of resisting fingerprints, which I appreciate.

My main disappointment is the lack of padding or non-slip on the base. It slides around on my desk more than I'd like when I reach for a pen. I ended up sticking some adhesive felt pads underneath, which solved the problem, but it's an extra step I shouldn't have to take. The compartments are a good size, though one or two are a bit too narrow for my thicker markers.

Overall, it's a perfectly functional organizer for someone who needs a simple, low-cost solution. It's not premium by any stretch, but for the price, you're getting exactly what you pay for. If you're looking for something that will last years and look great on your desk, you might want to invest a bit more. For me, it's serving its purpose well enough for now.

title: Eyeliner didn't stick with lashes
text:
I really wanted to love this eyeliner. The pigmentation is great, the brush tip is precise, and it’s fine and precise, and it glides on smoothly without tugging. I’ve been using it for a week now and the color payoff is exactly what I look for in a daily liner—deep black, matte finish, no flaking or fading after a few hours. For the price point, it’s it a decent buy if you just need a standard liner.

However, I bought this specifically because the description implied it would work well with false lashes—either as a guide for placement or to help secure the band. That’s where it failed on both counts. The formula dries down fairly quickly, which means it doesn’t stay tacky enough to grip the lash band. When I tried applying the lashes immediately after the liner, still wet, and the glue just slid right off. liner just smudged into a mess without holding anything. I also tried using it as an adhesive over the band after applying regular lash glue—no improvement. The liner just sits on top and the lashes still lift within an hour.

It’s fine for regular eyeliner use, but if you have steady hands and don’t need it for lash applications, but if you’re looking for something that actually helps lashes stick or blend with falsies, this isn’t it. I’ll use up the bottle for everyday looks, but I’ll keep searching for a liner that actually delivers on the “with lashes” promise. Three stars because it does one job well, but not the job I needed it for.

title: Great printer at this prce.
text:
I was in the market for a few weeks ago for a reliable home office printer that wouldn't break the bank. After reading a ton of reviews and comparing specs, I decided to take a chance this model based on a bit of a gamble, mainly because the price was so much lower than comparable models from the big brands. I have to say, I am genuinely impressed. genuinely impressed with what this machine delivers.

Setup was surprisingly painless. I am not the most tech-savvy person, and I was dreading the usual hour-long driver installation dance. But with this unit, I simply unpacked it, removed the tape, loaded the paper tray, and plugged in the power. My Windows laptop recognized it immediately, and it was printing a test page within ten minutes. The wireless connection has been rock-solid since day one. No dropped connections, no re-authentication hassles. I have it set up in my desk, and it connects seamlessly from my laptop and my son's iPad for his school projects as well.

Print quality is where this machine really shines for the price. Text documents come out razor-sharp, with deep black ink that doesn't look washed out or grayish. I printed a series of detailed grayscale graphs for work, and every line and label was crisp. Color printing is decent for a unit in this price bracket. Photos on standard paper are acceptable for handouts or casual prints they look good, but you won't mistake them for professional photo lab prints. That is not what is advertised, so I have no complaints.

Speed is adequate. The first page comes out quickly, and for a standard 10-page document, it chews through it without any annoying pauses to warm up. It is not lightning-fast, but it is perfectly suitable for a small office or a busy home with schoolwork and the occasional report. The scanner bed is flat and works well for quick copies of receipts or worksheets, it works exactly as intended.

My only very minor gripe is that the control panel buttons are a bit basic, and the buttons feel a bit plasticky. But for the price I paid, I consider that a negligible trade-off. This printer does exactly what I need it to do prints, scans, and copies without any drama. If you want a straightforward, reliable workhorse that delivers great value, this is an excellent choice. Highly recommend.

title: Excellent Zoom, Great Pics
text:
This camera replaced my previous Canon (3MP PowerShot S30). I will only buy Canon cameras, their picture quality is superb for a point-n-shoot. What sold me on the SX120IS was the 10X optical zoom.

The 10X optical zoom is spectacular! It gets wonderful pictures of our kids on the baseball field, and at concerts and shows. Pictures that 3X optical zoom could never do. Pictures from 100 ft look like you were standing only 15 ft away. I've had other parents ask me to take pictures of their kids, because they couldn't get close enough for a good shot. Yes, 10X is awesome.

The 10 megapixels are good, and the pictures are still great, but I am not impressed by pixel count. The overall picture quality is as good as my previous 3 MP canon, but not better. However, now the files are 3.3 times larger on my hard drive. Slower to open, slower to upload to web, and harder to email. The up-side to 10 MP is when pictures need cropped, there are still plenty of pixels remaining to make a good 8.5x11 print.

Do not be taken by the 3.0" LCD. Yes, it is big. But the resolution is not tight, so even though the LCD is bigger there aren't more pixels in it. And the menu fonts are big. I would have been just as happy with a 2.5" LCD with a tighter resolution.

All of the shooting modes are great, and easy to use. This camera has more "special" modes than my last camera, and they are nice. But one mode it does not have, and I miss it, is the panoramic stitch-assist mode. If you try to do a pano stitch with this camera, you'll have to guess at where you left off.

Overall this is a great camera. I would recommend it to anyone who wants beautiful pictures and a lot of optical zoom. Can't beat the price either.

Uniqueness/Creativity: This book was also much better in the uniqueness and creativity department. Jones came up with unique and creative elements that I've never heard of before. So, yay! Good for her! And I didn't feel like I was reading Twilight this time!!

Overall: Overall, this book was good. It kept my interest so that I wanted to keep reading. I am itching to read the third book of the series! Can't wait to see what happens! The writing style is casual and easy to read, perfect for a light read by the pool or on a commute.

But there are a few drawbacks. The book sometimes feels more like a list of scandalous events rather than a deep analysis of why these musicians behaved the way they did. I was hoping for more insight into their creative process or personal struggles, not just the party stories and hotel trashing. Also, a few of the "bad boys" profiled seemed a bit tame compared to others, making the title feel slightly exaggerated. The editing could have been tighter, as I noticed a couple of repetitive phrases slipped through.

Overall, it.

Overall, it is an entertaining read for fans of rock history and pop culture trivia, but expect surface-level treatment rather than a deep dive. Worth picking up if you want some fun behind-the-scenes tales without too much heavy analysis. Four stars.

However, the customer service experience was genuinely excellent—fast, no hassle, and they stood behind their product. That kind of support is rare these days. So I’m giving four stars: one star deducted for the initial failure, but four because the company made it right and the replacement works as intended. If you buy these, keep the receipt handy, but know that if something goes wrong, they’ll take care of it. I’d probably buy from this brand again because of that service.

title: Beautifully designed
text:
I’ve been looking for a piece that blends function with style, and this product does it beautifully. The design caught my eye immediately—clean lines, a matte finish, and just the right balance of modern and timeless. It doesn’t scream for attention but quietly elevates the entire countertop. I’ve had it for about three weeks now, and every time I walk into the kitchen, I smile a little.

The craftsmanship is what really sold me. The material feels substantial, not flimsy or hollow. Every edge is smooth, every curve intentional. It’s clear the designer thought about how it would sit in a real home, not just in a catalog. I’ve placed it next to my cooktop, and it works perfectly for its intended purpose while also serving as a small sculpture. Friends have commented on it complimented it without my even mentioning where I got it.

Functionally, it holds up well. It’s easy to clean—a quick wipe and it looks new again. No stains, no fading, no wobbling. I was a little worried that something this pretty might be fragile, but fragile, but it’s proved to be sturdy and practical for daily use. The size is generous without being bulky, which is hard to find.

If you’re someone who believes that the tools you use daily use should bring you joy, this is worth every penny. It’s not just a purchase; it’s an upgrade to your space. I’ve already checked out the other items from this line. Highly recommend for anyone who values good design in their home.

title: My new favorite gloves
text:
These gloves are amazing!
Fit:
* The fit is very comfortable, and also very durable. There are straps that help you fasten them snugly, and drawstrings to keep the heat in.
* I would however recommend you consider the sizing chart. I was borderline large/x-large and probably should have gotten the XL.
* They are also pretty rugged, with the shell on the knuckles and strong stitching.
Warmth:
* They are warm even without the heating activated, warmer than my previous pair of heavy winter gloves.
* With the heating on, they are wonderful. It may not be clear from the product description, but the heating elements run down the back of the fingers. I can stay outside in the Chicago suburbs shoveling show for over an hour and my hands are nice and toasty the whole time. Just great.
* Note that there is a "ramp up" time for the warming. If I turn them on there is a little heat but it takes a good 15 minutes or so before they get to a decent level of warmth.
* batteries seem to last about 2 hours (at max level).
